chunks.title: Yakkamon Publishes Its Launch Schedule — And the Free Mint Moved Two Weeks Earlier
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›The Launch Schedule, Finally

Event
The Launch Schedule, Finally

Aug 14, 2026

Yakkamon has published an Important Dates page — the first time everything between now and early access has been laid out in one place. It answers the question we've been fielding all month (when does the leaderboard lock?), narrows early access from "Q4" to November or December, and quietly moves the free mint two weeks earlier.

That last one matters more than it looks. If you were planning to get verified in late September, you have just missed the mint.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Publishes Its Launch Schedule — And the Free Mint Moved Two Weeks Earlier — The schedule
chunks.text:
The schedule

Event | Timing |

$FLOWER deposits — 3× points week | Live now (since 10 Aug), stepping down 0.2× per week to 1× — week 3 held at 2.8× after the week-2 pause |

Monster and egg utilities revealed | September |

Ronin free mint | Mid-September |

Free mint reveal | Mid-October — one month after the mint |

Leaderboard finalises | One week before early access launch |

Airdrop rewards sent out | Three days after the leaderboard finalises |

Early access launch | November / December — exact date to be announced |

Wave 1 enters | Early access launch day |

Wave 2 enters | One week after Wave 1 |

Wave 3 enters | One week after Wave 2 |

Wave 4 enters | Confirmed closer to launch |

chunks.title: Yakkamon Publishes Its Launch Schedule — And the Free Mint Moved Two Weeks Earlier — The five things that actually changed
chunks.text:
The five things that actually changed

1. The free mint moved from October 1st to mid-September. The second dev stream floated this as "likely"; it is now published on the official free mint page. Your verification deadline moved up with it.

2. You find out what you minted in mid-October, not at launch. The docs previously said all 10,000 mints stayed sealed until early access. They now reveal one month after the mint — roughly a month earlier than expected, and crucially before the leaderboard locks.

3. Early access is November or December. Q4 technically runs to 31 December, so this trims the window at the front but not the back.

4. The leaderboard lock has a position, if not a date. One week before launch. Until now the only official line was that it locks and that no date had been set.

5. Waves have a cadence. Wave 1 on launch day, Wave 2 a week later, Wave 3 a week after that. Wave 4 — ranks 20,001 to 100,000 — has no timing at all.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Publishes Its Launch Schedule — And the Free Mint Moved Two Weeks Earlier — Working out the real deadline
chunks.text:
Working out the real deadline

Nothing on this page is a date. Everything hangs off "early access launch", which is itself a two-month window. Chained together, though, it gives you a usable range:

If early access is… | Leaderboard locks | Airdrop lands | Days of grind left |

Early November | Late October | Very early November | ~75 |

Late November | Mid-November | Mid-to-late November | ~95 |

Mid-December | Early December | Early-to-mid December | ~110 |

So: somewhere between 11 and 16 more weeks of leaderboard, from today. Plan for the short end. If it runs long, you have banked points either way; if you plan for the long end and it lands early, you don't get the time back.

The deposit multiplier bottoms out long before the lock. It reaches 1× on 26 October — a week later than first scheduled, after week 3 was held at 2.8× following the week-2 deposit pause — still between one and six weeks before the leaderboard finalises. The most competitive stretch of the race is also the stretch where $FLOWER buys the fewest points. That asymmetry is the single most actionable thing on this schedule.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Publishes Its Launch Schedule — And the Free Mint Moved Two Weeks Earlier — What's good about this
chunks.text:
What's good about this

The lock is anchored, and you get notice. The team has committed to announcing the exact date with warning. Nobody wakes up to a board that closed overnight — which was the realistic fear when "it locks, date TBA" was all we had.

Rewards arrive before launch, not with it. Three days after the lock, four days before the doors open. You walk into early access already knowing what you're holding.

The mint reveal lands while you can still act. Mid-October is before the lock in every scenario above. If you open something good, you still have weeks to climb; if you open a common, you know to push harder on rank.

Waves 1 to 3 are close together. Rank 1,000 and rank 20,000 are two weeks apart in practice, not months. The penalty for finishing mid-table is much smaller than the rank gap suggests.

Utilities come before the lock. September for monster and egg utilities means you'll know what you're climbing toward before the climbing stops — the right order, and not the one this project expected.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Publishes Its Launch Schedule — And the Free Mint Moved Two Weeks Earlier — What's concerning
chunks.text:
What's concerning

Wave 4 has no timing whatsoever. That band is ranks 20,001–100,000 — the overwhelming majority of everyone who gets early access at all. "Confirmed closer to launch" could mean week four or it could mean February.

And deposited $FLOWER unlocks with access, not with launch. You can only spend or withdraw once you're in the game. For a Wave 4 trainer, that is an undated lockup on real money. If you have deposited meaningfully, the 20,000 line is worth more to you than it looks on the reward ladder.

Two official pages now disagree. The free mint page says mid-September; the Early Access and Rewards comparison table still says October 1st. Until that is reconciled, treat mid-September as the deadline and October 1st as the optimistic case — being early costs you nothing, being late costs you the mint.

A longer runway raises every cutoff. Sign-ups are still climbing and the deposit pool is already around 2.5M $FLOWER. Three or four more months means the points cost of rank 2,000, rank 5,000 and rank 20,000 all keep rising. A rank that looks comfortable in August is not a rank you can coast on into November.

You cannot time the end. The board gets hidden as launch approaches, and the lock date is announced rather than fixed. "Coast now, sprint at the end" fails twice: you won't know where the line is, and you won't know how long you have to reach it.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Publishes Its Launch Schedule — And the Free Mint Moved Two Weeks Earlier — What we'd do
chunks.text:
What we'd do

Treat 1 September as your verification deadline. Discord linked, X linked, wallet connected. Mid-September is the published mint window, not a promise about which half of it — and the whitelist is built before mint day, not on it.

If you are going to deposit, do it now. This is the only variable on the entire schedule that gets strictly worse with time, and it decays every single week. A deposit today is worth roughly three times the same deposit in late October.

Aim at a band edge, not a round number. The ladder is flat between edges — ranks 501 to 2,000 all receive Tide. The lines that pay are 2,000, 5,000, 20,000 and 100,000. Climbing from 1,800 to 700 gains you nothing at all.

Protect the nurture streak through mid-November. At day 30+ it's 70 points a week for a few seconds a day, and it's the only free source that compounds. Breaking it in October to "save effort" costs more than it saves.

Don't move a sealed mint before mid-October. If a market appears for unrevealed mints, remember that five Genesis Legendaries are in that pool of 10,000 and nobody — buyer or seller — can see which.

These are our readings, not announcements. The only fixed points are the ones in the official table above; every date derived from them in this article is arithmetic on a launch window that has not been set. We'll update this page as the exact dates land. The dates table, kept current →

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb

Guideline
Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb

Aug 3, 2026 · Updated Aug 14, 2026

Everything that matters in Yakkamon pre-registration comes down to one number: your points rank. It decides your permanent trainer number, whether you get early access at all, which wave you enter, and whether a Monster NFT lands in your wallet at launch.

Sign-up date decides none of that — it sets your Monster Egg tier and nothing else. Here's what the points are actually worth.

Only the top 100,000 trainers get early access. Pre-registering does not qualify you on its own. Below rank 100,000, you wait for full launch.

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — Daily nurture: how streaks work
chunks.text:
Daily nurture: how streaks work

Tap your egg 3 times to nurture it, once a day. Every nurture pays a base 5 points plus a streak bonus — the longer the run, the more each day is worth.

Streak | Points per day |

Day 1 – 2 | +6 |

Day 3 – 4 | +7 |

Day 5 – 9 | +8 |

Day 10 – 29 | +9 |

Day 30+ | +10 |

One nurture per day — the day rolls over at midnight UTC.

You always have 36 hours from your last nurture, so a single missed day need not break the run — though that only covers a whole missed day if you nurtured after noon UTC.

Leave it longer than that and the next nurture starts again at ×1.

A full week at ×30+ is 70 points.

Ninety days of perfect nurture is about 856 points. That's the whole grind from now to early access — worth knowing before you compare it to anything else on this page.

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — Every points source, with real numbers
chunks.text:
Every points source, with real numbers

Action | Points | How often |

Join the Discord | 10 | One time |

Connect X | 10 | One time |

Link a wallet | 10 | One time |

Discord contributions | 5 per post, 25 max | Capped |

Weekly X post | 20 first time, rising with streak | Once a week |

Daily nurture | 6 → 10 per day | Every day |

Refer a friend | 75 | First 5 instant; then the friend deposits 100 $FLOWER |

Ronin free mint | 250 | Once, mid-September only |

$FLOWER deposit | up to 70,000 | By amount |

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — $FLOWER deposits — the biggest lever by far
chunks.text:
$FLOWER deposits — the biggest lever by far

Deposits opened Aug 9 at 8:00 PM ET (the docs say 10 August — that's the UTC date for the same moment) and are live now. Every $FLOWER earns a point, and your deposited total unlocks bonus rates on top:

Single deposit | Points (opening week, 3×) | Size bonus |

50 $FLOWER | +150 | +5 (+10%) |

500 $FLOWER | +1,500 | +100 (+20%) |

5,000 $FLOWER | +15,000 | +2,000 (+40%) |

50,000 $FLOWER | +150,000 | +40,000 (+80%) |

The 3× applies only to the opening week. It drops 0.2× a week after — held at 2.8× in week 3, after the week-2 deposit pause — until it rests at 1×, so the same deposit made later is worth substantially less. The size bonus is rated per deposit — the full amount has to land in one transfer. The full schedule →

Your deposit address is issued on Aug 9 at 8:00 PM ET.

Send any amount on Base or Ronin — minimum 5 $FLOWER.

Points land in the week the deposit is confirmed. Deposits carry a weekly multiplier that starts at 3× and decays, plus a size bonus per deposit — so depositing early and in one transfer earns more than spreading it out.

All $FLOWER can be withdrawn once you gain access to the game.

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — $FLOWER deposits — the biggest lever by far
chunks.text: Be clear-eyed about this: a large $FLOWER deposit is worth tens of thousands of points — roughly 82× everything you'd earn from ninety days of perfect daily nurture. The top of this leaderboard will be decided by capital, not by grinding. That doesn't make the free actions worthless, and it doesn't put the Legendary bands out of reach either — realistically it's the top 100 that's a paid bracket, not the top 1,000. Referrals are uncapped at 75 points each, so around 66 of them match a 5,000 $FLOWER deposit — though past your fifth, each one now requires the friend to deposit 100 $FLOWER themselves. What capital buys outright is the very top; the rest is contestable. We're not financial advisors and we're not telling you to deposit; we're telling you what the numbers say.

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — What you can reach without depositing
chunks.text:
What you can reach without depositing

Roughly ninety days remain before early access. Playing free and consistently:

Source | Points |

90 days perfect nurture | ~856 |

All one-time quests (Discord, X, wallet, contributions) | 55 |

13 weekly X posts | 260+ |

Free mint, mid-Sept | 250 |

20 verified referrals (5 instant + 15 who deposit) | 1,500 |

Realistic total | ~2,900 |

Strictly free total (first five referrals only) | ~1,775 |

The free mint is the best value on the whole board. 250 points for one click in mid-September — more than three referrals, or 29% of a ninety-day nurture streak. If you do only one thing, do that.

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — What each rank gets you
chunks.text:
What each rank gets you

Points rank | Genesis Legendary |

1 – 3 | 🌩 Storm + ⬜ Echo |

4 – 10 | 🌩 Storm + 👻 Ghost |

11 – 50 | 🌩 Storm |

51 – 250 | ⬜ Echo |

251 – 500 | 👻 Ghost |

501 – 2,000 | 🌸 Bloom (called Tide until the September docs update) |

2,001 – 5,000 | Rare Egg |

5,001+ | ❌ Not eligible |

The top 2,000 trainers each receive one of the four Genesis Legendaries. Ranks 2,001–5,000 receive a Rare Egg. The wave bands are separate →

Twice as many Legendaries. They used to stop at rank 1,000 and now run to rank 2,000. Storm is new, sits above the old top tier, and only the top 50 are airdropped one. Monster utilities are due in September.

A, B and C are the same power level. Each letter hatches a different species with a different role — some battle, some farm utility — all at the same tier. The difference is scarcity by design: roughly 50 Egg As, 200 Bs, 260 Cs. So rank 1–100 is a rarer prize than 501–1,000, not a stronger one. More →

Two thresholds matter. Top 5,000 is where a Monster NFT starts. Top 100,000 is where early access starts. Everything in between is a question of which week you get in.

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — What doesn't count — and what can cost you rank
chunks.text:
What doesn't count — and what can cost you rank

Referral points are provisional until a final review. These are removed:

Unverified accounts — sign-ups that never complete verification.

Multi-accounting — alt accounts, throwaway emails, shared devices or wallets.

Bots and automation — bulk or scripted sign-ups.

Inactive sign-ups — accounts made purely to farm a bonus.

Removed referrals are deducted from your total, which can pull your trainer number down. Serious or repeated abuse can disqualify an account entirely. At 75 points each, chasing fake referrals is a poor trade against the risk — and the deposit requirement makes faking them expensive as well as risky.

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — Before the mint opens: get verified
chunks.text:
Before the mint opens: get verified

Update, 2 September 2026 — the mint changed shape. The official free mint page now gives a date and a structure: 14 September on the Ronin Launchpad, in five waves gated by your leaderboard rank at a 10 September snapshot — top 1,000 guaranteed, then ranks 1–10,000 (with 5 $FLOWER deposited), a Ronin-gamers wave, ranks 1–20,000 (with 5 $FLOWER), and ranks 1–50,000 for whatever is left. Outside Wave 1 it is fastest-click, one NFT per wave per account, and 68 Legendaries are hidden in the 10,000. The verification-only whitelist described below is the old plan — verification is still required, but rank and speed now decide your wave. The 250 points for minting still stand. Reveal is 14 October. The step-by-step mint guide → · The full wave table →

Updated 14 August. The free mint moved from October 1st to mid-September, so this deadline is now about two weeks earlier than it was. What else moved →

The free mint runs on a verified whitelist. Signing up isn't enough — an unverified account can't mint, however fast you are on the day. Complete verification well ahead of time so you're on the list, and you keep the 250 points too.

chunks.title: Early Access Leaderboard Guideline: How to Climb — The short version
chunks.text:
The short version

Nurture daily, ideally after 12:00 UTC so the 36-hour grace period actually covers a missed day.

Clear the one-time quests today — 55 points for a few minutes.

Mint in mid-September. 250 points, one click, best value on the board.

Refer real people only, and help them get started — 75 each. Your first five are instant; after that your friend needs to link a wallet and deposit 100 $FLOWER →. Fakes get deducted.

Deposits dominate the top of the board. Decide for yourself whether that's a game you want to play.

Top 5,000 for an NFT. Top 100,000 for early access.

Full detail lives on the Early Access page, and the FAQ covers rank, tier and wave in plain language.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full

Community
The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full

Aug 19, 2026

There is a new tab on the portal. Leaderboard ranks every $FLOWER deposit made on Base and Ronin, scored on the published point rules, and lets you find your own position in it. It also works out what the reward you are chasing would cost you today, and what the same reward costs if you leave it a month.

None of it comes from anyone’s word for it. Deposits are transfers on public blockchains, so they can be read directly, added up and ranked. That is all the page does.

And the first thing it shows is not a ranking at all. It is a count.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full — Fewer addresses have deposited than there are prizes
chunks.text:
Fewer addresses have deposited than there are prizes

At the time of writing, a little over 3,000 deposit addresses have ever received $FLOWER across both chains. The Genesis airdrop has 5,000 places.

Read carefully, because this is easy to overstate. It does not mean there are only 3,000 people in the race — there are hundreds of thousands of pre-registered trainers, and most of them have never deposited a thing. What it means is narrower and more useful: on deposit points alone, the board does not yet reach 5,000 names. The Tide band at rank 2,000 is full. The Rare Egg band at 5,000 is not, and cannot be, until more people deposit than have.

That is why the reward bands on the page read "Not full yet" rather than showing a number. There is no honest line to quote for a band nobody has filled.

The practical reading: the top of the real leaderboard is settled by money, because deposits scale in a way nothing else does. The bottom half of the reward zone is settled by everyone else — streaks, referrals and quests, none of which touch a blockchain.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full — What the page actually contains
chunks.text:
What the page actually contains

The full ranking. Every depositing address, its points, its $FLOWER total, how many separate deposits it made, and whether it used Base, Ronin or both. Paged a hundred at a time, with a jump-to-rank box.

Find your rank. Paste your deposit address and the page highlights your row, fills in your points, and tells you where you sit.

Plan your climb. Pick the reward you want, say how safe you want to play it, and it works out the deposit that would take you there, what that costs at the live $FLOWER price, and what the same target costs at a later multiplier.

What each prize takes. The current points line for every band from Storm at the top to the Rare Egg at 5,000, with the deposit needed to reach it from a standing start this week.

The address to paste is not your wallet. It is the deposit address Yakkamon issued to you — the same one on both chains. Open your account, scroll to QUESTS, click DEPOSIT on the early-deposit row, and keep scrolling: it sits near the bottom of that panel. It only ever receives your own deposits, so sharing it gives nothing away.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full — The formula, checked against a real account
chunks.text:
The formula, checked against a real account

points = amount × (week multiplier + bulk bonus)

The two bonuses add. They do not multiply, which is the single most common mistake in threads about this. At 2.8×, a 500 $FLOWER deposit earns 1,400 points plus a 100 bonus — the bonus is 20% of the deposit, not 20% of the points.

Before publishing any of this we tested it the only way that settles the question: we took a real account with a known score, rebuilt its deposits from chain data, and ran them through the formula. Five transfers, all in the opening week at 3.0×. The calculation returned 71,217 points. The game showed the same account 71,217 points. Not close — identical.

So the numbers on the page are not an approximation of the official scoring. They are the official scoring, applied to public data.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full — One transfer is worth more than ten
chunks.text:
One transfer is worth more than ten

The bulk bonus is rated on each transfer separately: +10% at 50, +20% at 500, +40% at 5,000, +80% at 50,000. We have been saying for two weeks that this makes one large early deposit worth considerably more than the same money dribbled in. The board is the first place you can see somebody actually do it.

One address on the ranking shows 50,200 $FLOWER and just over 190,000 points. Only one shape of deposit produces that total: a single 50,000 transfer in the opening week, catching the 80% band at 3.0×. Split into ten transfers of 5,000 the same money would have paid roughly 170,000. Split into a hundred transfers of 500 it would have paid about 160,000.

5,000 $FLOWER, deposited… | Points |

In one transfer, this week at 2.8× | 16,000 |

As ten transfers of 500, this week | 15,000 |

In one transfer, at the 1.0× floor | 7,000 |

As ten transfers of 500, at the floor | 6,000 |

Splitting costs you a little. Waiting costs you more than half.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full — What this board does not count
chunks.text:
What this board does not count

This is the important caveat, and it is on the page itself rather than buried here.

Nurture streaks and referral points do not exist on any blockchain. They live in Yakkamon’s own database, where nobody outside the team can see them. So every score on our board is a floor: everyone’s real total is higher, and the official ranking will differ from ours.

How much it differs depends on where you look. A trainer who has nurtured daily since launch and referred a handful of friends might be carrying somewhere north of a thousand points that we cannot see — enough to leap over a great many small depositors, and nowhere near enough to matter at the top, where single addresses hold six figures. Our board is therefore a good picture of the top of the race, a rough picture of the middle, and a poor one of the tail.

Treat these lines as a floor, not a verdict. If the page puts you at rank 900, your real rank is probably better than 900 and definitely not worse.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full — The clock behind all of it
chunks.text:
The clock behind all of it

The week multiplier started at 3.0× and steps down 0.2× every week to a 1.0× floor from 26 October — with one hold already on the books: depositing was paused during week 2, so week 3 stayed at 2.8× and the rest of the schedule shifted a week. Windows turn at 02:00 UTC, not midnight, which is worth knowing if you are timing a transfer against a deadline. The last window closes at 01:59 UTC on 16 November, and after that deposits stop earning anything at all.

The leaderboard that decides the airdrop locks one week before early access, which lands in November or December. Between now and then the lines on our page will only move upwards, because everyone else is still depositing. That is why the planner asks how much headroom you want: aiming at exactly today’s line is a plan to be overtaken.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full — What we still can’t tell you
chunks.text:
What we still can’t tell you

Your official rank. Only Yakkamon knows that, because only Yakkamon can see the off-chain points.

Where the 5,000th place actually sits. Not enough people have deposited to draw that line from chain data.

Which addresses belong to the same person. One trainer, one deposit address is the assumption. It is a reasonable one, and it is still an assumption.

Whether deposits will run the full window. They are scheduled to close on 16 November, but the multiplier reaches its floor three weeks before that — the cheapest points are the ones you buy today.

chunks.title: The Whole Deposit Board Is Now Public — And It Isn’t Full — Have a look
chunks.text:
Have a look

The board is at yakkamonworld.com/leaderboard, it recalculates from both chains through the day, and it is free and needs no account. If you find something in it that looks wrong, tell us — a public number that nobody checks is worth less than no number at all.

Built from public blockchain data. Deposits are read as transfers into each trainer’s own deposit address on Base and Ronin, then scored with the published point rules. This is our own work, not an official Yakkamon product, and it is not affiliated with the team.

chunks.title: Referral Rule Change: Friends Now Need 100 Points to Count
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›Referral Rule Change: Friends Now Need 100 Points to Count

Community
Referral Rule Change: Friends Now Need 100 Points to Count

Aug 5, 2026 · Updated Aug 7, 2026

Superseded — the rule changed again on 14 August. Discord and X no longer verify a referral at all. From your sixth onward, the friend must now link a wallet and deposit 100 $FLOWER of their own, and each counting referral pays 75 points rather than 30. The reasoning below still explains why the first tightening happened. The new rules →

The Yakkamon team has raised the bar for what counts as a valid referral. Your first five referrals still pay instantly — from the sixth onward, your friend must do all three of these before the points land: verify their Discord, verify their Twitter/X, and reach 100 points in their trainer dashboard. A sign-up on its own no longer pays.

chunks.title: Referral Rule Change: Friends Now Need 100 Points to Count — Why it changed
chunks.text:
Why it changed

Referral codes spread fast enough overnight to cause scaling problems, and in reviewing the surge the team found 4,783 accounts that had signed up using temporary-domain email addresses as part of a referral farming operation. Those accounts have been banned.

The 100-point requirement is the fix. It keeps the reward pointed at trainers who bring in real players, and makes bulk code-spamming worthless. The team also flagged that email codes and X connections were failing under load, with a fix rolling out.

chunks.title: Referral Rule Change: Friends Now Need 100 Points to Count — What it means in practice
chunks.text:
What it means in practice

Referrals still pay 30 points each and they're still uncapped. Referrals 1–5 are unaffected and land the moment your friend signs up. Beyond that, the work no longer ends at sign-up — and the 100-point step is the slow one, so here's how long it takes:

The three steps, in order of difficulty. Linking Discord and Twitter/X takes your friend about a minute each. Reaching 100 points is the one that takes real days — send them the quest list so they clear it fast.

Verify Discord — link a Discord account to their trainer profile.

Verify Twitter/X — link an X account to their trainer profile.

Reach 100 points in their trainer dashboard.

How your friend plays | Time to 100 points |

One-time quests first (55 pts), then daily nurture | About 7 days |

Daily nurture only, no quests | About 13 days |

Deposits even the 5 $FLOWER minimum | Considerably faster |

The one-time quests are the fast route: link a wallet, connect X, join the Discord and post five times is 55 points before they've nurtured once.

chunks.title: Referral Rule Change: Friends Now Need 100 Points to Count — What to do differently
chunks.text:
What to do differently

Stop treating a sign-up as the finish line. The highest-value thing you can do now is help the people you refer actually get started — send them the quest list, tell them to nurture daily, and check in during their first week.

The new arithmetic. Fifty sign-ups who never open the game are worth nothing. Twenty friends who play for a week are worth 600 points. Onboarding beats broadcasting.

chunks.title: Referral Rule Change: Friends Now Need 100 Points to Count — The rest of the rules are unchanged
chunks.text:
The rest of the rules are unchanged

Referrals are still reviewed before rewards are finalized, so the points stay provisional until then. These still don't count:

Unverified accounts — sign-ups that never complete verification.

Multi-accounting — alt accounts, throwaway or temporary-domain emails, shared devices and wallets.

Bots and automation — bulk or scripted sign-ups.

Inactive sign-ups — accounts created purely to farm a bonus, with no real activity. The 100-point rule now enforces this automatically.

Removed referrals are deducted from your total, which can lower your trainer number and your tier. Serious or repeated abuse can disqualify an account from pre-registration rewards entirely — as 4,783 accounts just discovered.

chunks.title: Referral Rule Change: Friends Now Need 100 Points to Count — Send this to anyone you refer
chunks.text:
Send this to anyone you refer

The free-to-play guide gets a new trainer past 100 points in their first week.

OPEN GUIDE →

Full rules on the pre-registration page, and every points value on the leaderboard guideline.

chunks.title: Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money — And Pay You 75 Points
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money

Event
Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money

Aug 14, 2026

Yakkamon has changed how a referral is verified for the second time in ten days — and this one is a different kind of change. The first tightened who counts. This one attaches a price.

chunks.title: Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money — And Pay You 75 Points — The three changes
chunks.text:
The three changes

| Before | Now |

How a referral verifies | Friend verifies Discord + Twitter/X, and reaches 100 points | Friend links a wallet and deposits 100 $FLOWER |

Points per referral | 30 | 75 |

First five | Instant on sign-up | Instant on sign-up (unchanged) |

The team's stated reason for dropping Discord and X is bluntly practical: bot accounts were clearing that bar in bulk, so the check was filtering nobody while flooding two community channels with fake members.

chunks.title: Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money — And Pay You 75 Points — The part that matters
chunks.text:
The part that matters

A 2.5× increase in points per referral reads like a win. It is, if you have the reach. But the verification bar moved from effort to money, and not your money — your friend's.

Under the old rule, a referral you'd persuaded to sign up could be walked to 100 points in about a week of free play. You could help. Under the new one, there is nothing you can do on their behalf: they need a wallet, they need 100 $FLOWER, and they have to send it themselves.

This changes what "free-to-play" means on this leaderboard. Referrals were the one uncapped free lever — the reason a determined player with reach could contest bands that otherwise belong to deposits. Past your fifth referral, that lever now runs on other people's money. Fifty referrals used to mean fifty conversations; it now means forty-five friends each spending 100 $FLOWER.

chunks.title: Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money — And Pay You 75 Points — What it does to the numbers
chunks.text:
What it does to the numbers

Player | Old total by mint | New total by mint |

No referrals | ~990 | ~990 (unchanged) |

Strictly free (first five only) | ~1,140 | ~1,365 |

50 referrals | ~2,490 | ~4,740 |

100 referrals | ~3,990 | ~8,490 |

Read the two middle rows together, because they're the whole story. The strictly free player — no money, and friends with no money — gains about 225 points from this change. The player who can find 45 friends willing to deposit gains about 2,250. The change is worth ten times more to the second player than the first.

chunks.title: Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money — And Pay You 75 Points — What's genuinely good about it
chunks.text:
What's genuinely good about it

It actually stops the farming. A hundred throwaway emails could clear Discord and X links. A hundred wallets each funded with 100 $FLOWER is 10,000 $FLOWER of real capital at risk of being stripped in review — a bad trade rather than a cheap one.

It stops polluting the community channels. Discord and X were being used as an anti-bot filter they were never suited for, and the cost was borne by everyone else in those channels.

The deposit isn't purely a cost to your friend. Their 100 $FLOWER earns them points too, at the current weekly multiplier and the +10% size bonus, and it stays theirs — spendable in-game or withdrawable once they have access. They're not paying you a fee; they're pre-loading their own balance.

75 points is a real rate. Against a 250-point free mint and roughly 6–10 points a day of nurture, one referral is now worth more than a week of daily play.

chunks.title: Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money — And Pay You 75 Points — What's concerning
chunks.text:
What's concerning

The leaderboard just got more expensive to climb, from both directions. Deposits were always the paid lane. Referrals were the free one. Both now route through $FLOWER.

It pushes the cost onto the person with the least information. You know why you're asking. Your friend is being asked to send 100 $FLOWER to a pre-registration for a game that hasn't launched, on the strength of your recommendation. That deserves care in how you ask.

Wallet-linked referrals interact badly with the multi-accounting rule. Shared devices and shared wallets are already grounds for removal. Funding a friend's wallet so they can clear the bar looks, in a review, a great deal like exactly that.

The docs haven't caught up. As of publication, docs.yakkamon.com still lists the old three-step rule. The updated rules are on yakkamon.com's own info pages. Two official sources, two different rules — assume the stricter one applies.

chunks.title: Referrals Now Cost Your Friend Money — And Pay You 75 Points — What we'd do
chunks.text:
What we'd do

Use your five instant referrals first. They're free, they're unconditional, and at 75 points they're now worth 375 — more than a month of nurture. Anyone who hasn't used them is leaving the easiest points on the board.

Past five, ask people who were going to deposit anyway. Someone already planning to put $FLOWER in loses nothing by routing 100 of it through your link. Someone who wasn't is being asked for real money.

Be straight with them about what you're asking. Explain that it's their wallet, their money, that it stays theirs, and that it earns them points too. Don't front the 100 $FLOWER for them.

Recalculate your target. If your rank plan assumed 50 free referrals, that plan needed rewriting this morning. The revised free-to-play numbers →

Nothing here is retroactive as far as we can tell. Referrals already credited under the old rule have not been announced as under review because of this change — though referral points have always been provisional until the final review. We'll update this page if that changes.

chunks.text:
Read next

The previous referral change — the one this replaces

The free-to-play guide, with revised totals

The launch schedule — how long you have to climb

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers — And Your Resources Won't Travel for Free

Event
Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers — And Your Resources Won't Travel for Free

Aug 28, 2026

The Yakkamon team has published the next guide in its series, this one on expansion and Regions. It is shorter than the economy post and reads, on a first pass, like flavour: more land, more resources, more monsters to hunt. Read it a second time and it is the most structural thing they have published about how the idle half of the game is actually laid out — and one line in the middle of it, about "logistics", quietly changes how a farm in this game has to be planned.

Here is what the seven points say, what follows from each, and what it does to the advice already on this site.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — The seven points, in plain terms
chunks.text:
The seven points, in plain terms

# | What the post says | New? |

1 | Your Region is made of tiles. You gather resources to unlock more, and each tile you claim expands what you can do and how much you can run at once. | New (tiles as a cap on concurrency) |

2 | Tiles are not just space. A tile can hold fresh resources, room to build, or a hunting area where wild Yakkamon roam. | New (hunting areas are tiles) |

3 | Grow your starting Region far enough and you unlock entirely new Regions. | Confirms, with a gate |

4 | Each new Region brings its own resources and its own monster types. A Water Region has water hunting areas full of Yakkamon you could not catch back home. | New (first named Region type; monsters are Region-local) |

5 | You keep everything you unlock. Old Regions stay part of your operation, which means learning to automate and manage your Yakkamon across several Regions at once. | New |

6 | Managing that spread is "the real puzzle". Moving and sharing resources between your Regions becomes a core part of the strategy — "the trainers who master logistics get ahead". | New (and the big one) |

7 | Regions get progressively bigger each time you expand, and more roll out in upcoming Chapters. | Confirms the chapter cadence |

Points 3 and 7 restate things the dev streams had already said — one Region per Chapter, roughly, across the first year. Points 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are the ones to read twice.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — Layer one: tiles are a cap on how much you can run, not just where
chunks.text:
Layer one: tiles are a cap on how much you can run, not just where

Everyone assumed expansion meant land. The post says something more specific: each tile "expands what you can do and how much you can run at once". That second clause is a concurrency limit. Your tile count decides how many jobs, stations and plots can be live in parallel, which makes it the hard ceiling on the idle half of the game — above the storage bin, above the monster count, above everything.

That reframes an argument we made ten days ago. In The Game That Starts the Next Morning we said your storage bin is your ceiling: past a point, adding monsters to a job only fills the bin faster and wastes more. That is still true within a tile. But the number that decides how many bins you have in the first place is tiles — and the price of a tile is paid in the resources those bins hold. The loop closes on itself: gathered resources buy tiles, tiles raise how much you can gather, and the only thing that breaks the loop is running out of monsters of the right type to fill them.

The one number we have. The starter expansion button reads 10 Wood + 1 Stone. Nothing else about tile pricing is public — not how the cost climbs, not how many tiles a Region holds, not how many parallel jobs one tile adds. Anyone who tells you the "optimal expansion order" today is guessing.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — Layer one, continued: every tile is a choice
chunks.text:
Layer one, continued: every tile is a choice

Point 2 gives tiles three possible contents: resource nodes, build space, or a hunting area. That is an opportunity cost the earlier material never had. A tile spent on a hunting area is a tile not spent on plots, and vice versa.

It also changes what a hunting area is. The launch screenshot showed a sign with an entry cost of 5 berries, which read like a toll on a public place. The post makes hunting areas land you claim first and pay to enter second. Two costs, not one — and the first of them competes directly with your production.

Read that against plot groups from the third dev stream, where growing tiles come in groups and upkeep scales more slowly than production within a group. If tiles are the unit and groups are how plots pack onto them, then the team's stated push — invest deep in a group before spreading — now has a second reason behind it: the tiles you would spread onto are the same tiles you need for hunting areas.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — Layer two: a new Region is a bootstrapping problem
chunks.text:
Layer two: a new Region is a bootstrapping problem

Point 4 is where the post connects to the rule that already shapes this game. Type locking says each resource can only be gathered by the right type. The Regions post says each Region has its own resources and its own monster types, and that the monsters of a Water Region live in that Region's water hunting areas.

Put those together and arriving somewhere new does not make it productive. The sequence for a Water Region, as far as the published rules allow us to reconstruct it:

Unlock the Region by growing your starter Region — paid for in grasslands resources.

Claim at least one tile there as a water hunting area — paid for in resources you had to bring, because you cannot gather water materials yet.

Send a monster in with lures and berries from home, and catch your first water type.

Only now can the Region's own resources be gathered, and only by that monster and whatever you catch after it.

Every step before the last one is funded from somewhere else. And the economy post closed the shortcut a week ago: basic monsters have limited tradeability, so you cannot buy a water type on day one and skip the expedition. A Region is a place you have to earn your way into with the Region before it. That is elegant design, and it is also the reason the first player into each Region will be weeks ahead of the second, not hours.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — Layer three: chapters, and why the newest Region will always matter most
chunks.text:
Layer three: chapters, and why the newest Region will always matter most

Point 7 says two things. More Regions arrive with Chapters, which matches what the team said on stream about pairing each Chapter with a new Region and new species. And Regions get progressively bigger each time you expand.

The second part is a hint about where the meta will live. If each Region is larger than the last, the newest Region is always the largest reservoir of tiles, and therefore of concurrency. Combined with seasonal monster drops that players race to claim, the shape of a Chapter launch looks like this: everyone who can reach the new Region rushes it, because it is both the biggest and the only place the new monsters are. The Regions you already own become the supply chain that funds that rush — which brings us to the line that matters.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — The line that matters: your resources do not travel for free
chunks.text:
The line that matters: your resources do not travel for free

Point 6 is written casually and it is the most important sentence in the post. Moving and sharing resources between your Regions "becomes a core part of the strategy", and "the trainers who master logistics get ahead".

That sentence has no meaning if your inventory is global. You do not "move" wood between two places that share a bag. The only reading under which logistics is a puzzle at all is that resources are held per Region: what a monster gathers in the grasslands stays in the grasslands until something carries it out.

What that implies, if it holds. A second Region is not simply more production. It is production that lands in the wrong place, plus a transport step to get it where it is needed. Every new Region has to be fed before it feeds you. Bin caps almost certainly apply per Region, so a Region you stop visiting fills up and stops earning, exactly like an unvisited bin. And any tool that plans production for this game will need a transport cost in it — a number that does not exist yet.

The post is silent on the mechanism. Whether moving resources costs time, a monster's stamina, a building on each end, a fee, or nothing beyond a tap; whether monsters themselves move freely between Regions; whether the Trade menu is also the transport layer — none of it is stated. What is stated is that it will be hard enough to separate good players from average ones. We would read that as: it costs something real.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — The line that matters: your resources do not travel for free
chunks.text: This is also where specialisation stops being a slogan. The economy post said to expect trainers to specialise and trade for what they do not produce. If type-locked materials exist only in one Region and shipping them is a cost, then a trainer who has settled the Water Region and one who has not are natural counterparties. Logistics is what turns the two-economies design into an actual market.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — Nothing sunsets — and that is a cost as well as a promise
chunks.text:
Nothing sunsets — and that is a cost as well as a promise

Point 5 is framed as reassurance: old Regions do not get left behind. It is also the sentence that tells you how your attention scales. Two things already on the record make an unattended Region expensive: bins cap and stop banking output, and plots degrade so that what does run, runs worse. A Region you stop visiting does not pause. It decays, and it does so on every Region you own at once.

The team's own answer is in the same sentence: learn to automate. That word is doing a lot of work. The work cycle already repeats and restarts itself, so "automate" may mean nothing more than assigning monsters well and trusting the loop. But it lands a week after an economy post that said out loud that the gathering loops can be automated, and that the tradeable economy is walled off from them for that reason. The consistent reading of both posts is that the team expects the idle half of this game to run with very little of you in it, whether through in-game tooling or otherwise, and has designed the economy so that this is fine. Anyone planning to hand-manage four Regions from a phone should hear that.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — How this squares with the dev stream
chunks.text:
How this squares with the dev stream

On 21 August the team drew a line between gathering regions you build on and hunting regions you explore, and Adam described hunting regions as the deliberate Pokémon reference — the feeling of arriving at the beach and sensing new possibilities. The Regions post instead puts hunting areas on tiles inside a Region.

We do not think those contradict each other. The most likely reading is that a hunting area is a tile you claim within a Region, and that the "arriving at the beach" moment is your first visit to a new Region's hunting areas rather than a separate map. But the post does not say so, and we have rewritten the Regions system page to flag the two framings side by side rather than pick one.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — What we changed on the site
chunks.text:
What we changed on the site

The Regions, Tiles & The World system is rewritten around the three layers.

A new Logistics Between Regions system — the 23rd — carries the per-Region inference and everything that is unpublished about transfers.

The field guide, the quick-reference table and the not-confirmed list on both gameplay pages now carry the tile, Region and logistics facts, each sourced to this post.

Four new answers in the FAQ.

The field guide poster is redrawn: nineteen gameplay-only panels, with Regions & Tiles and Logistics new, and the platform and pre-registration panels dropped.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — What's genuinely good here
chunks.text:
What's genuinely good here

Expansion is paid in the free layer. Tiles cost gathered resources, which the economy post walled off from money. You cannot buy land with $FLOWER on the published rules, so the idle half stays a game of time and roster rather than wallet.

Regions are earned, not sold. The Region gate is "grow your starting Region", not a mint. Progress carries progress.

Type locking finally has a map to live on. Region-local monsters give the type system a reason to exist beyond a refusal message.

Logistics is a skill expression the idle half was missing. A farm that runs itself has no way to reward a better player. A supply chain does.

Nothing you build becomes obsolete. Old Regions feed new ones, which is the opposite of the throwaway starter zone most games ship.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — What to be wary of
chunks.text:
What to be wary of

The transfer mechanic is the whole game and it is unpublished. A free tap and a two-hour caravan produce completely different games, and the post picks neither.

Attention scales with Regions. Decay applies everywhere you own at once. The more you unlock, the more a weekend away costs.

First-mover gaps compound per Region. Each Region is bootstrapped from the last, so a lead in the grasslands becomes a bigger lead in the Water Region, and bigger again in the one after. Wave 1 has more to gain from this post than from anything in the economy one.

"Automate" is undefined. If it means in-game tooling, fine. If it means the team expects scripts to run the idle half, that has consequences for what a free player's time is worth.

The stream and the post use "region" differently. Until the team reconciles hunting regions with hunting-area tiles, any guide that speaks confidently about "the hunting region" is ahead of the source.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — What to actually do
chunks.text:
What to actually do

Plan tiles as a budget, not a map. Every tile is a hunting area or production. Decide the split before you spend the first 10 Wood.

Treat your starter Region as the factory for everything after it. Grasslands output funds the Water Region's first tiles, lures and berries. Under-build it and every later Region starts late.

Catch one of every local type before you leave. You cannot buy your way into the next Region's type, and the monsters that work it live there. Breadth at home is what makes the next Region open quickly.

Assume a transport cost until told otherwise. Build the second Region to be self-sufficient in its own materials as early as possible, rather than shipping everything in.

Do not build a Region planner yet. Tile pricing, Region gates and transfer costs are all missing. We are not building one either, and that is the honest reason.

chunks.title: Yakkamon's World Has Three Layers: Tiles, Regions and the Logistics Between Them — The five questions we'd put to the team
chunks.text:
The five questions we'd put to the team

Is inventory per Region, and if so, what does moving a stack of resources between Regions cost?

Do monsters move between Regions freely, or is a squad assigned to one?

What is the condition that unlocks the second Region — tile count, quest, level or payment?

Do storage bins and plot degradation apply per Region, and does an unvisited Region keep degrading?

Is a "hunting region" from the dev stream the same thing as a hunting-area tile in this post?

All five are answerable today, and the first one alone would tell tool-builders whether a production planner for this game is a spreadsheet or a routing problem.

Source and standing. This is our reading of an official Yakkamon guide on expansion and Regions, published on the team's own channels. The seven points above are summarised in our words; every inference — per-Region inventory most of all — is ours, is marked as such, and is not endorsed by anyone. If the transfer mechanic turns out to be a free tap, we will say so on this page.

The Reward Egg Ladder Just Changed

Aug 12, 2026 · Updated Aug 14, 2026

Yakkamon has rewritten the airdrop ladder. The top 10 now receive two monsters, a new top-tier monster called Storm was added above the old ladder, and Legendary monsters now run twice as far down the leaderboard. Here’s the new table, what it means for where you are, and what the team says about it.

chunks.title: The Reward Egg Ladder Just Changed — What It Means For Your Rank — The new ladder
chunks.text:
The new ladder

Points rank | Reward egg |

1 – 3 | 🌩 Storm + ⬜ Echo |

4 – 10 | 🌩 Storm + 🌸 Bloom |

11 – 50 | 🌩 Storm |

51 – 250 | ⬜ Echo |

251 – 500 | 🌸 Bloom |

501 – 2,000 | 🌊 Tide |

2,001 – 5,000 | Rare Egg |

5,001+ | ❌ No reward egg |

Only the top 10 receive two eggs. Ranks 11 to 5,000 receive one, decided on points alone.

chunks.title: The Reward Egg Ladder Just Changed — What It Means For Your Rank — What the team says
chunks.text:
What the team says

"Nothing has been nerfed." The team’s stated position is that this update does not nerf an existing Yakkamon for a leaderboard ranking. Lower-tier Yakkamon utility is being lifted to match previously expected traits, and more monsters are being released — so every rank still gets the kind of utility it was already in line for, and far more players end up rewarded with powerful monsters. Monster utilities are due to be published in September.

chunks.title: The Reward Egg Ladder Just Changed — What It Means For Your Rank — What changed, in plain terms
chunks.text:
What changed, in plain terms

Every band either kept the monster it was in line for — with its utility lifted — or moved up into a better one.

If you finish at… | Was in line for | Now receives |

Rank 2 | Legendary Egg A | 🌩 Storm + ⬜ Echo |

Rank 40 | Legendary Egg A | 🌩 Storm |

Rank 100 | Legendary Egg A | ⬜ Echo |

Rank 300 | Legendary Egg B | 🌸 Bloom |

Rank 600 | Legendary Egg C | 🌊 Tide |

Rank 1,500 | Rare Egg | 🌊 Tide — Rare becomes Legendary |

Rank 3,000 | Rare Egg | Rare Egg — utility lifted |

Legendary supply roughly doubled. Legendary monsters used to stop at rank 1,000 and now run to rank 2,000 — from about 1,000 in supply to about 2,010. Storm is new and was added above the ladder rather than pushing anyone down it. The four Genesis Legendaries →

chunks.title: The Reward Egg Ladder Just Changed — What It Means For Your Rank — What to do about it
chunks.text:
What to do about it

If you were targeting a Legendary, the line moved out from rank 1,000 to rank 2,000 — twice as reachable as before.

If you were targeting top 5,000, nothing changed — ranks 2,001–5,000 still receive a Rare Egg.

If you are outside 5,000, the position is unchanged: no reward egg, but early access still runs to rank 100,000.

Nobody should act on utility assumptions yet. Monster utilities land in September.

The full rank ladder and the pre-registration guide are both updated, and the early-access wave bands are unchanged — this update covered reward eggs only.

chunks.title: We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction, With The Real Numbers
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction

Community
We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction

Aug 12, 2026 · Updated Aug 14, 2026

Correction, 14 August 2026. An earlier version of this article said the 12 August update halved Legendary supply and cost around 500 trainers a tier. Both claims were wrong. Legendary supply roughly doubled, and no band lost out. The original text is gone rather than quietly patched, and what follows is the corrected analysis. We’ve explained the mistake at the end.

On 12 August Yakkamon rewrote the airdrop ladder, and on 14 August published the monster names behind it. Taken together the picture is clear, and it isn’t the one we described first time.

If you just want the analysis of the change itself rather than our correction, the full breakdown is here.

chunks.title: We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction, With The Real Numbers — 1. The four Genesis Legendaries
chunks.text:
1. The four Genesis Legendaries

The founding set now has names, and the old "Legendary Egg A/B/C" labels are retired. The mapping matters, because it’s what makes the change legible:

Monster | Ranks | Supply | Previously called |

🌩 Storm | 1 – 50 | 50 | new — added above the ladder |

⬜ Echo | 1–3, 51 – 250 | 203 | Legendary Egg A |

🌸 Bloom | 4–10, 251 – 500 | 257 | Legendary Egg B |

🌊 Tide | 501 – 2,000 | 1,500 | Legendary Egg C |

Supply figures are official. The airdrop totals 5,010 Monster NFTs across 5,000 trainers — the extra ten are the second monsters going to ranks 1–10.

chunks.title: We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction, With The Real Numbers — 2. Legendary supply doubled
chunks.text:
2. Legendary supply doubled

This is the number we got backwards, and it’s the heart of the update.

| Before 12 Aug | Now | Change |

Legendary monsters | 1,000 | 2,010 | +1,010 |

Rare Eggs | 4,000 | 3,000 | −1,000 |

Total airdrops | 5,000 | 5,010 | +10 |

Legendary monsters used to stop at rank 1,000. They now run to rank 2,000 — twice as far down the leaderboard. A thousand trainers who were in line for a Rare Egg now hold a Genesis Legendary instead.

chunks.title: We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction, With The Real Numbers — 3. Nobody lost a band
chunks.text:
3. Nobody lost a band

We checked every band against the original ladder. Not one came out worse.

Rank | Was in line for | Now receives | |

1 – 3 | Legendary Egg A | 🌩 Storm + ⬜ Echo | ⬆️ two monsters |

4 – 10 | Legendary Egg A | 🌩 Storm + 🌸 Bloom | ⬆️ two monsters |

11 – 50 | Legendary Egg A | 🌩 Storm | ⬆️ upgrade |

51 – 100 | Legendary Egg A | ⬜ Echo | same monster, utility lifted |

101 – 250 | Legendary Egg B | ⬜ Echo | ⬆️ moved up a tier |

251 – 500 | Legendary Egg B | 🌸 Bloom | same slot, utility lifted |

501 – 1,000 | Legendary Egg C | 🌊 Tide | same slot, utility lifted |

1,001 – 2,000 | Rare Egg | 🌊 Tide | ⬆️ Rare becomes Legendary |

2,001 – 5,000 | Rare Egg | Rare Egg | unchanged — utility lifted too |

1,200 ranks improved. 3,800 held their slot with utility lifted. Zero moved down.

So "nothing has been nerfed" holds up. We questioned that framing when the bands first changed, on the basis that it was a claim about power made about an update we read as being about scarcity. With the names published, the claim is simply accurate — and the scarcity moved in players’ favour rather than against them.

chunks.title: We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction, With The Real Numbers — 4. Storm is the real story
chunks.text:
4. Storm is the real story

The genuinely new thing here is a monster that sits above the previous top tier.

Until now the site’s position — from the team’s own statements — was that the Legendaries are all the same power level, differing in species and role rather than strength. Storm is the exception. It’s described as the newest in the set and the hardest to earn, and the only route to being airdropped one is a top-50 finish.

That creates something the old ladder didn’t have: a genuine gradient at the very top. Previously ranks 1 and 99 received an identical reward, which made the difference between them meaningless. Now the top 50 is a distinct prize and the top 10 is distinct again.

It also quietly addresses a design weakness we flagged. After the first dev stream we argued the flat top-100 band was a real problem. Adding a scarcer monster above the ladder fixes it without breaking the same-power-level design that the other three rest on.

chunks.title: We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction, With The Real Numbers — 5. What it means for your target
chunks.text:
5. What it means for your target

The Legendary line moved out, not in. It was rank 1,000. It’s now rank 2,000 — a materially easier target than before, and the single most useful change for anyone planning.

Top 50 is the new stretch goal, and the only way to a Storm.

Top 5,000 still matters — it’s the last band that receives an airdrop at all.

Early access is unchanged at the top 100,000, and remains very reachable free.

The flat zones are worth knowing, because points spent inside a band buy nothing: 501–2,000 all receive Tide, and 2,001–5,000 all receive a Rare Egg. Deposit timing →

chunks.title: We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction, With The Real Numbers — 6. What we still don’t know
chunks.text:
6. What we still don’t know

Monster utilities land in September. Everything about what these creatures actually do — battle, farm utility, or something else — is unpublished. "Utility lifted" is the team’s description and can’t be verified until then.

It also isn’t stated whether the two monsters at ranks 1–10 are separate creatures or one reward described in two parts, though the phrasing points at separate.

chunks.title: We Got The Reward Ladder Wrong — The Correction, With The Real Numbers — How we got it wrong
chunks.text:
How we got it wrong

Worth explaining, because it’s the second correction on this site in a fortnight and you should know how much weight to put on our numbers.

The 12 August update published bands without monster names. It listed ranks 501–2,000 as receiving "Rare Egg A" and 2,001–5,000 as "Rare Egg B". We read "Rare" as a tier below Legendary — which it plainly implies — and concluded that ranks 501–1,000 had dropped out of the Legendary bracket, and that Legendary supply had roughly halved.

The names published on 14 August show that band receives Tide, a Genesis Legendary. Our reading was wrong, and the arithmetic built on it was wrong with it.

In hindsight the lesson is a simple one: we ran the numbers confidently on labels we didn’t understand, when the honest move was to say the labels were ambiguous and wait. We’d rather publish this than leave the original up.

chunks.text:
Just want the new table?

The ladder itself, without the commentary.

THE NEW LADDER →

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon

Guideline
The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon

Sep 2, 2026

▶ Prefer to watch? The free-mint stream recapped in 4 minutes ↗
On 14 September, 10,000 hidden Genesis Yakkamon go up for free on the Ronin Launchpad. You pay gas and nothing else, you mint blind, and every one of them is revealed on 14 October. Hidden in the pool are 68 Legendaries. This is the one page to read before then: what the mint is, which waves you can join, exactly what to do before 10 September, and how mint day itself works.

Everything here comes from the official free mint page, the Important Dates page and the free-mint dev stream. Where we add our own reading, we say so.

Three dates, in order. 10 September — the leaderboard snapshot that builds the whitelists. 14–18 September — the mint, one wave a day. 14 October — the reveal. If you only remember one: your rank on the 10th decides which waves you can mint in, and nothing you do after that changes it.

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — The mint at a glance
chunks.text:
The mint at a glance

What | 10,000 Genesis "Hidden" Monster NFTs — each with unique stats, usable in the game |

When | 14 September, then one wave a day to 18 September |

Where | The Ronin Launchpad, on the Ronin blockchain |

Cost | Free — you only pay network gas, in RON |

Who | Whitelisted trainers by leaderboard rank at the 10 September snapshot, plus a Ronin-gamers wave |

How many | One NFT per wave per account — you can mint in every wave you qualify for |

Hidden inside | 68 Legendaries (3 Storm, 5 Echo, 10 Ghost, 50 Bloom), 50 Rares, 9,882 Uncommons |

Reveal | 14 October — every NFT at once, one month after the mint |

Points | Minting earns 250 pre-registration points on your leaderboard score |

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — The five waves — and which ones are yours
chunks.text:
The five waves — and which ones are yours

The mint runs as five whitelisted waves. Each opens to a different slice of the leaderboard, and the supplies add up to 11,000 against a 10,000 collection, so later waves only get what earlier waves leave. Wave 1 is the only guaranteed one; from Wave 2 onwards it is fastest-click while supply lasts.

Wave | Date | Supply | Who can mint |

Wave 1 | 14 Sept | 1,000 | Top 1,000 whitelisted trainers — guaranteed mint, at your own pace |

Wave 2 | 15 Sept | 3,000 | Ranks 1–10,000 with a 5 $FLOWER minimum deposit |

Wave 3 — Ronin wave | 16 Sept | 2,000 | Active Ronin gamers, on a whitelist built by the Ronin team |

Wave 4 | 17 Sept | 5,000 | Ranks 1–20,000 with a 5 $FLOWER minimum deposit — ends early if the 10,000 sell out |

Wave 5 | 18 Sept, 00:00 UTC | Remaining | Ranks 1–50,000 |

Ecosystem airdrop | TBD | 1,500 | Sent manually: 1,000 to top Ronin spenders, 500 to $FLOWER ecosystem players |

Only Wave 5 has a published opening time (00:00 UTC). The others have dates but no clock time yet, and the stream described the later-wave timings as tentative — watch the official channels for the exact hour before each one.

Because the brackets nest, a high rank unlocks every lower wave too. Find your row:

Your rank on 10 Sept | Waves you can mint in | Max NFTs | What you need |

1 – 1,000 | 1, 2, 4, 5 | 4 | 5 $FLOWER deposited for Waves 2 and 4; Wave 1 is yours regardless |

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — The five waves — and which ones are yours
chunks.text:
1,001 – 10,000 | 2, 4, 5 | 3 | 5 $FLOWER deposited, and be online the moment Waves 2 and 4 open |

10,001 – 20,000 | 4, 5 | 2 | 5 $FLOWER deposited for Wave 4; Wave 5 needs no deposit |

20,001 – 50,000 | 5 only | 1 | Be ready at 00:00 UTC on 18 September, if any supply is left |

50,001+ | None from the leaderboard | — | Wave 3 only, if the Ronin team’s gamer list includes you |

Ronin gamer (any rank) | 3, plus whatever your rank gives | +1 | On Ronin’s whitelist — the Yakkamon leaderboard is not the criterion |

Our reading of the maths. Waves 1 and 2 together account for 4,000 of the 10,000, and Wave 2 alone is 3,000 mints for up to 10,000 eligible trainers — most of them will not get one. Wave 4 is the realistic wave for ranks 1,001–20,000 — but if Waves 1–3 sell out it opens with 4,000 left, not 5,000, and Wave 5 may open to nothing. Treat every wave past the first as a race, and every earlier wave you qualify for as the one that matters.

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — Before 10 September: the checklist
chunks.text:
Before 10 September: the checklist

The snapshot is the real deadline. Four things need to be true by then.

Pre-register and verify. An unverified account is not on any whitelist, however high its rank. If you haven’t signed up yet, register at yakkamon.com (that link carries our code YAKKA-UDBVPX) and complete verification the same day.

Be at the rank you want. The lines that matter are 1,000, 10,000, 20,000 and 50,000. Check your position on our deposit leaderboard and inside yakkamon.com — if you sit just outside a line, the fastest way across is a single $FLOWER deposit, made early in the week. This week’s multiplier is 2.6×, and the week of 7 September (the snapshot week) is 2.4×. The schedule →

Deposit at least 5 $FLOWER if you are counting on Wave 2 or Wave 4. It is not a fee — the 5 $FLOWER is fully withdrawable or spendable once the game is live — it exists to make multi-accounting expensive. Any deposit of 5 or more on Base or Ronin qualifies, and it earns points on top. Where to get $FLOWER →

Set up a Ronin wallet. The mint is on Ronin only. Base deposits count for points and for the 5 $FLOWER condition, but the wallet that mints has to be a Ronin wallet. Install the official Ronin Wallet (browser extension or mobile app), write down the recovery phrase offline, and link that wallet to your Yakkamon account.

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — Before 10 September: the checklist
chunks.text: Minting is worth 250 points. That is more than three referrals, for one click, and it lands on your score before the leaderboard finalises — so the mint can improve the rank your airdrop is paid on, not just get you an NFT.

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — Mint day: step by step
chunks.text:
Mint day: step by step

Get RON for gas in advance. Gas is paid in RON, Ronin’s native token. A small amount covers a mint; buy it inside the Ronin Wallet or on an exchange that supports Ronin withdrawals, and do it days ahead rather than at wave open.

Open the Ronin Launchpad at marketplace.roninchain.com/launchpads — type the address yourself or use the link from the official docs, never one from a DM or a reply.

Connect the Ronin wallet you linked to your Yakkamon account. The whitelist is checked against the wallet, so a different wallet, even one you own, may show as not eligible.

Be there before your wave opens. Outside Wave 1 supply goes to the fastest clicks. Have the page loaded, the wallet unlocked and the gas already in it.

Mint, then approve the transaction in your wallet. Wait for it to confirm on-chain — the hidden NFT will appear in your Ronin wallet and on the Ronin marketplace under your address.

Come back for each wave you qualify for. One NFT per wave per account. A top-1,000 trainer with 5 $FLOWER deposited has four chances across 14–18 September.

Wave 1 is the exception. If you are in the top 1,000 your mint is guaranteed and you can take it at your own pace on the 14th. Everyone else should assume their wave empties in minutes.

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — What is hidden inside
chunks.text:
What is hidden inside

Every mint is a sealed pull from the same 10,000. Here is what the pool holds, per the official page and the Yakkapedia:

Tier | In the mint | Chance per mint | Utility (from the Yakkapedia) |

Storm (Legendary) | 3 | 0.03% | Stormcharged — Yakkamon in range work twice as fast, large area |

Echo (Legendary) | 5 | 0.05% | Yakkamon in range produce double resources, small area |

Ghost (Legendary) | 10 | 0.1% | Unsleeping — always at maximum stamina on the farm, small area |

Bloom (Legendary) | 50 | 0.5% | Regenerates a share of max HP every combat turn |

Rare | 50 | 0.5% | Normal working monster, rare tier |

Uncommon | 9,882 | 98.8% | Normal working monster |

So roughly one mint in 147 is a Legendary, and one in 85 is Rare or better. The honest expectation is an Uncommon with unique stats — a usable worker from day one, and an NFT you can hold, trade or sell. Anything above that is a bonus. Utilities, names and artwork can still be tweaked before launch, per the docs’ own caveats. What each Legendary does →

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — After you mint
chunks.text:
After you mint

It is tradable straight away. Hidden NFTs can be bought and sold on the Ronin marketplace before the reveal, and after it. Selling blind means selling a 0.68% Legendary ticket; buying blind means paying for one.

Reveal is 14 October. All 10,000 flip at once, together with the 1,500 ecosystem airdrop — 11,500 revealed in total. That is before the trainer leaderboard finalises, so you will know what you hold while you can still climb.

Deposit it into the game at early access (November/December). The marketplace, auctions and $FLOWER withdrawals open at Chapter 0, one month after early access.

This is the ongoing Yakkamon collection. Monsters released later join the same collection, so your mint is not a one-off "genesis" side set.

The mint and the airdrop are separate. The 10 September snapshot builds the mint whitelists only. The Genesis airdrop to the top 5,000 keeps running on the live leaderboard, finalises one week before early access, and lands automatically three days later — no mint, no wallet action. You can win both.

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — Stay safe: it is free, so anyone charging is a scam
chunks.text:
Stay safe: it is free, so anyone charging is a scam

The only cost is RON gas. A "mint page" asking for a price, a deposit or an approval of your whole wallet is not Yakkamon.

Mint only at marketplace.roninchain.com. Bookmark it now. Fake launchpads with near-identical addresses appear around every popular mint.

The team will not DM you a link, an early-access mint or a "whitelist fix". Nobody legitimate ever needs your recovery phrase.

Keep only the RON you need for gas in the minting wallet if you are new to Ronin, and read every wallet prompt before you approve it.

chunks.title: The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide: How to Mint Your Hidden Yakkamon — Mistakes that will cost you a mint
chunks.text:
Mistakes that will cost you a mint

Verifying after 10 September. The lists are already built.

Sitting at rank 1,004 or 10,050 on the 9th and assuming it holds. It is a deposit week; ranks move.

Depositing 5 $FLOWER on the 11th for Wave 2. It needed to be there for the snapshot — do it now.

Having $FLOWER on Base but no Ronin wallet linked. Points yes, mint no.

Buying RON at 23:58 UTC for a 00:00 wave. Exchanges and bridges take time.

Minting once in Wave 1 and going to bed. You may have three more waves to claim.

Tip
Tip: Deposit on Ronin If You Haven’t Yet

Sep 2, 2026

$FLOWER is the same token at the same contract address on Base and Ronin, and a deposit earns identical points on either chain. Until now the choice didn’t matter. It does now, for one reason: the free mint on 14 September happens only on Ronin, and gas for it is paid in RON.

chunks.title: Tip: Deposit on Ronin If You Haven’t Yet — Why Ronin, if the points are the same
chunks.text:
Why Ronin, if the points are the same
A Base wallet cannot mint, however verified the trainer behind it is. Whoever deposits on Ronin has already installed the Ronin Wallet, already swapped inside it, and already holds RON — the three things a Base depositor has to set up separately in the week the mint opens. The 5 $FLOWER condition for Waves 2 and 4 is met on either chain; only the minting wallet has to be Ronin.

chunks.title: Tip: Deposit on Ronin If You Haven’t Yet — How to do it
chunks.text:
How to do it
Install the official Ronin Wallet, write the recovery phrase down offline, and fund it with a little RON. Swap for $FLOWER inside the wallet — check the contract address against the official deposits page first, since a copycat pair exists on Base — and send it to your own deposit address in one transfer. Then link that wallet to your Yakkamon account before the 10 September snapshot, and leave the RON in it: that is your mint-day gas.

chunks.title: Tip: Deposit on Ronin If You Haven’t Yet — Already on Base?
chunks.text:
Already on Base?
Nothing to undo. Your points are safe, the 5 $FLOWER condition is met, and there is no need to bridge anything — your deposit address accepts both chains and the mint doesn’t care where your $FLOWER sits. You just need a Ronin wallet as well: set one up, fund it with RON, link it, mint from it. This tip is not saying Base deposits are worth less, and it is not saying to move $FLOWER between chains. It is only saying the next deposit is easier on the chain you will be minting on anyway.

class="wrap article-head">

Tip
Tip: Nurture After 12:00 UTC, Every Day

Aug 5, 2026

Everyone knows about the 36-hour grace period on nurture streaks — the one that means a single missed day shouldn't break your run. It works less often than people assume.

chunks.title: Tip: Nurture After 12:00 UTC, Every Day — Two clocks, not one
chunks.text:
Two clocks, not one
The game day rolls over at midnight UTC, and separately you get 36 hours from your last nurture before the streak resets. 36 hours is a day and a half, and whether that spare half-day actually covers a missed day depends entirely on what time you tapped.
Nurture at 08:00 UTC and your window closes at 20:00 tomorrow — still inside tomorrow, so you have to nurture again. Nurture at 20:00 UTC and it closes at 08:00 the day after — you can miss a whole day and survive.

chunks.title: Tip: Nurture After 12:00 UTC, Every Day — The cutoff is noon UTC
chunks.text:
The cutoff is noon UTC
Noon plus 36 hours lands exactly at the end of the next day. Before noon, no safety net. After noon, a real one. That's 8:00 AM in New York, 1:00 PM in London, 8:00 PM in Manila and 9:00 PM in Tokyo — so in the Americas you're mostly covered already, while east of London a morning nurture leaves you no slack at all.

chunks.title: Tip: Nurture After 12:00 UTC, Every Day — Why bother
chunks.text:
Why bother
Breaking a streak doesn't cost you one day. You drop from 10 points a day back to 6 and need 29 days to climb back — roughly 44 points on top of the day you missed. An unbroken run to the free mint is worth about 526 points.
