chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›Tip: Deposit Your $FLOWER Early, In One Transfer

Tip
Tip: Deposit Your $FLOWER Early, In One Transfer

Updated Aug 7, 2026

This tip previously said the opposite. It used to advise splitting deposits across weeks, because the bonus appeared to follow your cumulative deposited total. The first dev stream on 6 August described a different structure, and the advice reverses with it. We've rewritten it rather than quietly editing. What changed →

If you're planning to deposit $FLOWER, two bonuses decide how many points you get — and both reward the same behavior: deposit early, and in single larger transfers.

chunks.title: Tip: Deposit Your $FLOWER Early, In One Transfer — The weekly multiplier decays
chunks.text:
The weekly multiplier decays

Every week of the deposit window carries a multiplier. The opening week pays 3× — three points per $FLOWER — and the rate then falls by 0.2× every week until it settles at 1×.

Week 1 | Week 2 | Week 3 | Week 6 | Week 12+ |

3.0× | 2.8× | 2.8× | 2.2× | 1.0× |

Updated 24 August — week 3 stays at 2.8×. Depositing was paused during week 2, so rather than dropping to 2.6×, the team held the week 3 multiplier at 2.8×. The 0.2× weekly step resumes from week 4, which pushes every later week — and the 1.0× floor — one week later than originally scheduled.

Which means the same 5,000 $FLOWER is worth 17,000 points in the opening week and 7,000 once the multiplier bottoms out — a 10,000-point difference for waiting.

The multiplier applies to points, not to your balance. You keep the same $FLOWER and can still withdraw it once you have game access. What's tripling is what that deposit is worth on the leaderboard.

The team was explicit about why: they want points earned early, rather than a stampede on the last day before launch.

chunks.title: Tip: Deposit Your $FLOWER Early, In One Transfer — The size bonus is per deposit
chunks.text:
The size bonus is per deposit

Separately, larger deposits earn bonus points — calculated per transfer, not on your running total.

Single deposit | Bonus rate | Bonus points |

50 $FLOWER | +10% | +5 |

500 $FLOWER | +20% | +100 |

5,000 $FLOWER | +40% | +2,000 |

50,000 $FLOWER | +80% | +40,000 |

The rate doubles at every step. Ten deposits of 500 earn ten 20% bonuses; one deposit of 5,000 earns a single 40% bonus, which is worth a thousand points more.

Two half deposits are worth less than one whole one. Sending 25 $FLOWER and then another 25 does not reach the 50 tier. It has to be a single transaction.

chunks.title: Tip: Deposit Your $FLOWER Early, In One Transfer — What to actually do
chunks.text:
What to actually do

Deposit as early in the window as you're comfortable with. Week one is worth the most, and it only goes down.

Send it in one transfer, so the size bonus applies to the full amount.

Don't hold back for a strong finish. Waiting to watch the leaderboard and depositing at the end is exactly what this structure penalises — and the leaderboard gets hidden near launch anyway.

Minimum is 5 $FLOWER, on Base or Ronin. Points land in the week the deposit confirms.

Check against your own dashboard. These rates come from the official deposit panel, including the week-3 hold at 2.8×. The week boundaries are our own calculation from the 10 Aug opening, so confirm there if you're close to a week edge.

None of this is advice about whether to deposit at all. $FLOWER is real money and that call is yours. This is only about timing, for people who have already decided.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot
chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›Nobody Noticed the Number in the Background

Event
Nobody Noticed the Number in the Background

Aug 18, 2026

There is a storage bin sitting at 20/20 in Yakkamon's own screenshot — full, stopped, banking nothing, on a world the studio has been playing for over a week. It is the most useful thing in the image, and it is in the background behind the thing we were meant to be looking at.

Most Yakkamon reveals so far have been artifacts: a roster sheet, a mock-up of a HUD, a comparison table in the docs. Useful, but static. They tell you what the game will contain, not what it's like.

The Updates panel is different. It's a screenshot of a live world with a history — a news feed with five dated posts, a named author, working bin counters in the background, and a button that takes you straight into the activity being announced. It leaks more about how Yakkamon actually operates than anything since the dev streams.

The official Updates panel. The interesting part is behind it.

Here's everything we can reasonably read from it, what it confirms, what it changes, and where we're still guessing.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — 1. There is a live-ops system, and it's been running for at least nine days
chunks.text:
1. There is a live-ops system, and it's been running for at least nine days

Post | Age |

New Wild Yakkamon | 4 hours ago |

The Lumber Yard Opens | 1 day ago |

Weekly Rewards Rotate | 2 days ago |

Referral Boxes | 5 days ago |

Welcome, Trainers | 9 days ago |

Two things follow. First, Yakkamon has an in-game news channel, not just a Discord and a docs site — announcements arrive where you're playing, authored and dated, with a call to action attached.

Second, and more interesting: "Welcome, Trainers" sitting at nine days old implies a world that has been up and accumulating events for at least that long. That's a build being lived in, not a demo assembled for a screenshot.

Be careful with that inference. Timestamps in a test environment can be seeded, and a staging world is not the launch world. But the mundane spread of ages — four hours, one day, two days, five days, nine days — is what a real feed looks like, not what someone types into a mock-up.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — 2. Hunting has an economy, and it isn't free
chunks.text:
2. Hunting has an economy, and it isn't free

The open post is the most useful text Yakkamon has published about moment-to-moment play. Four new yakkamon have appeared in the Grasslands, and trainers are told to prepare bait and monsters, bring berries, and rest their squad first.

Unpack that and three separate mechanics fall out.

Bait is a thing. Hunting isn't walk-up-and-catch. You bring something to attract or hold a creature, and berries appear to be it — or at least one form of it.

Berries are a hunting consumable. We already knew the Hunting Area charged 5 berries to enter. That looked like a toll. It now looks more like ammunition: berries are what you spend to hunt at all.

Your squad needs to be rested before you go. Stamina isn't only a gathering constraint. A tired squad is a squad that can't hunt, which means the idle half and the active half of the game compete for the same resource.

That last point is the one with teeth, and we'll come back to it.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — 3. Bins cap at 20, and at least one is sitting full
chunks.text:
3. Bins cap at 20, and at least one is sitting full

Look past the panel at the world behind it. Four storage counters are visible in the overworld, reading 3/20, 20/20, 0/20 and 0/20, with a lone 5 on a structure to the right.

Two counters, side by side. One is at 3/20. The other has stopped.

This is the first time the bin cap has been visible in a live world rather than in a mock-up, and it confirms the number we'd been treating cautiously: 20 in the early game.

It also shows something we'd only argued theoretically. One of those bins is at 20/20 — full, stopped, banking nothing. In a screenshot presumably taken by someone from the studio, on a world they've been playing for over a week, a bin is sitting at max wasting production.

That's the whole storage bin argument in one number. Overflow isn't a hypothetical inefficiency for careless players. It's the default state of any bin you don't empty, and it happens to everyone.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — 4. Grasslands is the first named region
chunks.text:
4. Grasslands is the first named region

Every region we knew about was exotic: deserts, volcanoes, fire regions, oceans. Grasslands is new, and its name plus its role — the place where four new creatures are announced for general hunting, with berries as the stated cost — makes it look like the starter region.

That matters for a reason that isn't obvious. Type locking means each region's materials are gated to types. If Grasslands is the opening area, its type requirements are the ones every new trainer meets first, and the ones that shape which creatures are worth catching in week one.

We'd guess Grass types are well served there. That is a guess, and we're flagging it as one.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — 5. The menu has changed
chunks.text:
5. The menu has changed

Earlier screenshots showed six buttons: Squad, Items, Quests, Shop, Trade, Log. This one shows five: Squad, Shop, Quests, Trade, News.

So Log has become News, and Items has gone — most likely folded into the item bar along the bottom of the screen rather than deleted. Small, but it tells you the UI is still moving, which is a useful corrective to reading any screenshot as final.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — 6. The other four headlines each imply a system
chunks.text:
6. The other four headlines each imply a system

The Lumber Yard Opens — a named production building, and the word "opens" implies structures unlock over time rather than all being available from the start.

Weekly Rewards Rotate — a weekly reward cycle already live. That's the strongest evidence yet for the team's stated consideration of weekly seasons rather than the quarterly cadence in the docs.

Referral Boxes — referrals pay out as in-game boxes, connecting the pre-registration referral system to something you actually open at launch.

Welcome, Trainers — the world's opening post.

And the author line reads Pumpkin Pete, a name Sunflower Land players will recognize. Whether that's a shared character, a studio pen name, or an in-world NPC voice, it's a deliberate thread back to the parent game.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — What this changes about our own advice
chunks.text:
What this changes about our own advice

We argued a few days ago that the opening week should be played breadth-first: catch widely before you catch well, because type locking means a narrow roster caps what you can produce at all.

We still think that's right. But this screenshot adds a cost to it that we didn't account for.

Going wide means hunting a lot. Hunting costs berries, and it costs squad stamina — and squad stamina is the same pool your gatherers draw from. So every hunting trip is paid for twice: once in consumables, once in production your monsters didn't do while they were out being tired.

The revised advice: go wide on types, but fund it. Get a berry supply running before you go on a catching spree, and stagger hunts so your whole squad isn't resting at once.

A trainer who hunts constantly with no berry economy behind it will end week one with a broad roster, an empty larder and four bins at max. That's a worse position than a narrow roster that's actually producing. We'd rather revise this now than let the original stand unqualified.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — What we still can't tell
chunks.text:
What we still can't tell

Whether bins upgrade past 20, and what it costs. A 120 cap has appeared in mock-ups; nothing here confirms it in a live build.

What bait actually does. Berries are named, but whether bait improves catch rates, attracts specific species, or is simply an entry fee is unstated.

How much stamina a hunt costs, or how long a rest takes. Without those, the trade-off above can't be quantified.

Whether this is the launch world. Everything here could be an internal build with tuning that never ships.

What the four new Grasslands yakkamon are. No names, no types, no images.

chunks.title: Nobody Noticed the Number in Yakkamon's Own Screenshot — The honest summary
chunks.text:
The honest summary

Nothing in this screenshot is a headline announcement. There's no date, no reward, no rule change. It's an interface with some numbers in the background.

But it's the first look at Yakkamon as a running system rather than a set of planned features — a world with a history, a news feed, an economy of consumables, and a bin quietly sitting full because someone forgot to empty it.

For a game whose early access window is November or December, a build that's been lived in for over a week is a better signal than any roadmap.

Compiled from an official screenshot. This is our reading, not an announcement — several conclusions above are inferences and are labelled as such. Mechanic-by-mechanic references, with sources named per figure, are in the field guide.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Referral Code: Pre-Registration Opens to Everyone Aug 4 — Yakkamon access code vs referral code — what's the difference?
chunks.text:
Yakkamon access code vs referral code — what's the difference?

Both phrases point at the same box on the sign-up screen, but the codes come from different places.

An access code is what Sunflower Land players have been claiming from the Yakkamon sign next to Stella in the Plaza. Those unlocked in waves by Bumpkin Level, starting at Level 150+ and finishing with Level 20+ on Aug 2.

A referral code — sometimes called a trainer code — comes from a player who has already registered. That's the route that opens on Aug 4, and it has no requirements attached at all. So if you've been searching for a "Yakkamon code" and coming up short, this is the one you want.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Referral Code: Pre-Registration Opens to Everyone Aug 4 — How to get a Yakkamon referral code
chunks.text:
How to get a Yakkamon referral code

There are three easy ways:

Ask a friend who has already signed up. Every registered trainer has a code to share.

Use this portal's code. It's YAKKA-UDBVPX — type it into the trainer code screen when you register at yakkamon.com.

Ask in the community. Plenty of trainers drop codes in our Telegram chat.

Worth knowing: whoever's code you use earns 75 points — instantly if you're one of their first five, otherwise once you've linked a wallet and deposited 100 $FLOWER of your own — for a verified referral. Using ours supports this portal; using a friend's does exactly the same for them. It makes no difference to you either way — so use a friend's if you have one.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Referral Code: Pre-Registration Opens to Everyone Aug 4 — How to register with a referral code, step by step
chunks.text:
How to register with a referral code, step by step

1. Wait for 8:00 PM ET on Aug 4. Referral codes don't work before that moment, no matter where you got yours.

2. Go to yakkamon.com. That's the official game site — this portal is a fan project and can't register you itself.

3. Enter your code on the "Enter Trainer Code" screen exactly as it was given to you, then press Confirm.

The same screen Sunflower Land players have been using — a referral code goes in the same place.

That's the whole process. There's no purchase, no wallet connection, and no gas fee at this stage.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Referral Code: Pre-Registration Opens to Everyone Aug 4 — What pre-registering actually gets you
chunks.text:
What pre-registering actually gets you

Signing up locks in your Monster Egg tier, which is handed out purely in sign-up order: the first 10,000 trainers get Platinum, then Gold, Silver, Bronze and Basic as the numbers climb toward 500,000. Registering earlier gets you a better egg — that's the one thing the clock decides.

It also puts you in position for the two dates that follow: the free Genesis Monster mint in mid-September (open to pre-registered trainers only, you cover just the network fee) and Early Access in November or December 2026, when the game actually opens — staged by wave, with your rank deciding which one you're in.

Registering does not reserve you a leaderboard place. Your trainer number, your wave into Early Access, and the Genesis airdrop — 5,000 free monsters, with Legendaries for the very top — are all decided by points earned after you sign up. A Basic egg holder who shows up daily will finish above a Platinum holder who never comes back.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Referral Code: Pre-Registration Opens to Everyone Aug 4 — Why the official docs say "August 5th"
chunks.text:
Why the official docs say "August 5th"

Because they're quoting the UTC date. 8:00 PM ET on Tuesday Aug 4 is midnight UTC, which is already Wednesday Aug 5 in London and everywhere east of it. Same instant, two calendar dates — if you're in the Americas, the evening you want is Tuesday the 4th.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Referral Code: Pre-Registration Opens to Everyone Aug 4 — Yakkamon referral code FAQ
chunks.text:
Yakkamon referral code FAQ

Do I need a Sunflower Land account?

No. That requirement disappears entirely on Aug 4. It's a big shift — the roughly 295,000 Sunflower Land players below Level 20 become eligible at the same moment as everyone who has never touched the game.

Do I need a crypto wallet to pre-register?

Not to pre-register. A Ronin wallet matters later for the free mint and the airdrop, but the sign-up itself just needs a code. The FAQ walks through wallets and gas when you're ready for them.

Where do I enter my Yakkamon code?

On yakkamon.com, on the "Enter Trainer Code" screen — the same field for access codes and referral codes alike.

Does a referral code cost anything, or expire?

They're free, and you use one only once, at sign-up. You don't need to collect several.

What does the person who referred me get?

75 points per verified referral. The first five are instant; from the sixth onward the friend must link a wallet and deposit 100 $FLOWER of their own — a sign-up alone no longer pays, and linking Discord and X no longer counts. Only genuine referrals count — removed ones are deducted, and abuse can disqualify an account outright. The referral rules spell this out.

Can I still register after Aug 4?

Yes — pre-registration doesn't close on Aug 4, it opens. But because eggs go out in sign-up order, the difference between registering on the 4th and registering in September is a real one.

chunks.text:
class="wrap article-head">
Home›News›Eighteen Yakkamon, No Names

Event
Eighteen Yakkamon, No Names

Aug 17, 2026

An official roster sheet has surfaced showing eighteen Yakkamon side by side — the first proper look at the creatures themselves rather than the systems around them.

Updated 31 August — twenty-two. The fourth row gains a fourth creature: a pastel moth with patterned wings. The other twenty-one are unchanged and in the same order, and two slots in the fourth row still sit empty. Still no names, no types, no rarities — and at twenty-two of the expected 50–60, the revealed share stays at roughly two-fifths.

Updated 25 August — the sheet has grown to twenty-one, with one correction. A newer official sheet starts a fourth row with three new creatures — a pink owl, a blossom-pink creature carrying a small bowl, and a pale hooded creature — and a follow-up version corrects one of the original eighteen: the badger's slot now holds an upright purple-and-cream creature with a red nose. The other seventeen are unchanged and in the same order. Still no names, no types, no rarities. Against the expected 50–60 at launch, the revealed roster moves from about a third to roughly two-fifths. Everything below stands as written on 17 August — including the original sheet, badger and all.

The updated sheet: twenty-two portraits, with the fourth row filling in. Tap to open it full size.

chunks.title: Eighteen Yakkamon, No Names — What the Roster Sheet Tells Us — The original sheet, as published
chunks.text:
The original sheet, as published

Eighteen portraits, three rows of six. Tap to open it full size.

chunks.title: Eighteen Yakkamon, No Names — What the Roster Sheet Tells Us — The one number that gives it context
chunks.text:
The one number that gives it context

The team has said to expect roughly 50 to 60 Yakkamon at launch. Against that, eighteen is somewhere around a third of the early access roster — enough to read the art direction, nowhere near enough to plan around.

That ratio is the useful bit. It means roughly two out of every three creatures you'll meet in early access are still unseen, so any conclusion drawn from this sheet about the shape of the roster — which types dominate, how the rarities distribute, what a good starting team looks like — is being drawn from a third of the evidence.

chunks.title: Eighteen Yakkamon, No Names — What the Roster Sheet Tells Us — What's actually on the sheet
chunks.text:
What's actually on the sheet

Portraits, and nothing else. There are no names, no types, no rarities, no stats and no indication of which are common and which are rare. The line-up leans heavily on real animals given a chunky, expressive treatment: bears, foxes, pandas, badgers, ducks, frogs, deer, horses, a boar. Two are clearly dragons, and at least one is plant-based rather than animal — a sprouting seed creature with leaves for a head.

If there's a design thesis visible here, it's that Yakkamon is going recognisable rather than abstract. These read as animals first and monsters second, which is a different instinct from the creature-collectors it'll inevitably be compared to.

The missing field that matters most is type. Because of type locking, a monster's type decides which resources it can gather at all — a Grass type gathers Wood, a Fire type is refused outright. So a portrait tells you almost nothing about whether you'd want one on a farm. Until types are attached to these eighteen, nobody can say which are worth chasing.

chunks.title: Eighteen Yakkamon, No Names — What the Roster Sheet Tells Us — What we're not going to do with it
chunks.text:
What we're not going to do with it

Guess types from colours. The red one might be Fire. It might also be a Rock type that happens to be red. Colour-to-type mapping is a convention borrowed from other games, not something Yakkamon has stated.

Guess rarity from position. Grid order on a character sheet is usually production order or an artist's arrangement, not a tier list. Reading the top-left slot as "the starter" or the bottom-right as "the legendary" is inventing a system that isn't there.

Attach names. None are published, and the team has said monster names aren't final and may end up community-influenced. Any name circulating for these right now is somebody's guess.

Assume these are the Genesis Legendaries. Storm, Echo, Bloom and Tide are pre-minted airdrop rewards with a separate supply. Nothing on this sheet identifies which, if any, of these eighteen they are.

chunks.title: Eighteen Yakkamon, No Names — What the Roster Sheet Tells Us — What it does confirm
chunks.text:
What it does confirm

Modestly but genuinely: the creatures exist, they're finished to a consistent standard, and the art style is settled rather than in flux. For a project whose early access window is November or December, a coherent roster sheet a third of the way to the launch count is a reasonable place to be.

It also lines up with the September commitment on monster and egg utilities. If utilities land as promised, that's the release where these portraits start to mean something — types, roles, and what each actually does on a farm.

We'll update this as names and types land. The roster now sits on our Gameplay page and in the field guide, and we'll attach details to each creature as the team publishes them rather than before.

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide
chunks.text:
class="gg-sec" id="two-halves">
01

THE SHAPE OF IT

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Two halves, one game
chunks.text:
Two halves, one game

Half of Yakkamon plays itself. Half of it needs you — and each half feeds the other.

The idle half

Your monsters farm, gather and produce around the clock. Set them up, walk away, come back to progress. This keeps running even when the game is closed, so you log back in to a pile of stuff waiting for you.

The active half

You go out hunting rare creatures, craft your gear, and fight other trainers in the arena. This only moves when you're actually playing — and better hunts feed a better farm.

LIKE THISYour farm is a slow cooker that keeps going all night. Hunting is the trip to the shops for better ingredients.

02

THE ENGINE

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — The core loop
chunks.text:
The core loop

Six things you do over and over. Every system in the game bolts onto this circle.

Catch — head into the wild and hunt Yakkamon. Every one you catch joins your roster.

Work — send them out to gather resources. They repeat the job automatically, even offline.

Collect — their haul stacks up in a storage bin. Tap the bin to move it into your inventory.

Craft — turn raw resources into gear, items and buildings, including the gear that catches rarer monsters.

Maintain — feed and heal your monsters, and refertilise plots that have degraded. New as of 21 August, and it means you can't set this up once and walk away.

Level up — higher-level Yakkamon gather faster. Better gear plus a better team means you go catch something rarer, and you're back at step one.

LIKE THISIt's a snowball. Small team, small resources, small upgrades, slightly bigger team. Do that twenty times and you have an empire.

03

THE ROSTER

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Your Yakkamon
chunks.text:
Your Yakkamon

Expect roughly 50–60 species at launch — and four separate things decide whether one individual is worth keeping.

Twenty-two of the expected 50–60, as of 31 August — portraits only, with names and types still to come. What can and can’t be read into it →

Its type
Type decides what it can gather. A Grass type gathers Wood. A Fire type can't — the game refuses outright. Thirteen types at launch, one per monster; dual types come later.

Its stats
Every monster rolls slightly different stats. Two of the same species won't be identical, so it's worth hunting the same one again for a better roll.

Its rarity
Rares sit in tiers, and certain rares are more powerful than other rares in the same tier.

Its utility
Every monster carries a boost. Legendaries have a named one; Rares and Uncommons roll theirs at random, separately from their stats — so great stats and a great utility on one monster is the jackpot. No wearable gear exists to make up the difference.

The second dev stream filled in the machinery underneath: monsters have real genetics and base stats, traits are randomly rolled and define your build, and there are breeding lines with degradation but no hard cap, with evolutions planned. The team put roll predictability at roughly 80–90%.

LIKE THISThink trading cards. Same picture on the front, better numbers on the back — and that's the one everybody wants.

04

THE TIERS

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Rarity, decoded
chunks.text:
Rarity, decoded

Two corrections from 21 August that reframe the whole roster.

Rarity is set at species level
Every individual of a species shares its tier. There is no rare version of a common monster and no legendary variant of an ordinary one. Grinding commons hoping for a lucky upgrade roll is not a strategy that exists.

Rarer is not simply stronger
The best commons beat middling rares and roughly match a low-end legendary on raw stat outlay. What rarity buys is a higher ceiling as the monster levels, scarcer utility, and traits no other tier can access.

The three tiers
Legendary — pre-minted, fixed scarce supply, minted as NFTs, exclusive traits. Rare — time or event limited, issued as SFTs, supply set by how hard players hunt. Common — plain game assets with no token behind them.

How you get them
Hunting is the primary route at every tier. Rares can appear in any hunt; legendaries lean on events, specific conditions and tournament wins.

Utilities & auras — what the Legendaries actually do

Legendary | Supply | Utility | Airdrop ranks |

🌩 Storm | 75 | Stormcharged — Yakkamon within range work 2× as fast (large AOE) | 1–50 |

⬜ Echo | 275 | Yakkamon within range produce double resources (small AOE) | 1–3, 51–250 |

👻 Ghost | 400 | Unsleeping — always at maximum stamina on the farm (small AOE) | 4–10, 251–500 |

🌸 Bloom | 2,000 | Regenerates a % of Max HP every combat turn | 501–2,000 |

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Rarity, decoded
chunks.text:
Small AOE vs large AOE
Small touches only the job the monster stands on — assign it to a tree and the two or three trees beside it get the effect. Large covers a whole section of the farm and every Yakkamon working there.

They stack, some multiply
Some utilities are additive, some are multiplicative with each other. Storm + Echo is the confirmed combo: twice the speed on top of double the output.

Rares and Uncommons roll theirs
No utility is listed for them because each one is randomly rolled at generation, independently of species and stats. Keepers are the ones that rolled both well.

Numbers not yet published
The utilities are descriptive text. Radii, percentages and every Rare/Uncommon utility are still being balanced — and will be, the team says, right up to release.

Tide is gone. The docs renamed two of the four: the 251–500 Legendary formerly called Bloom is now Ghost, and the 501–2,000 Legendary formerly called Tide is now Bloom. Same monsters, same boosts — renamed to match their types. The full Genesis table →

LIKE THISA first-team squad player can outperform a benched international. The badge tells you the ceiling, not the current form.

05

THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Type locking
chunks.text:
Type locking

Every resource can only be gathered by the right type, so your roster decides what you're able to gather at all.

Resource | Who can gather it | Status |

Wood | Grass types | CONFIRMED |

Wood | Fire types — blocked. In-game message: "Fire type cannot harvest wood!" | BLOCKED |

Stone | Type not yet announced | UNKNOWN |

Berries / crops | Type not yet announced | UNKNOWN |

Region materials | Each Region has its own resources and its own monster types — the Water Region is the named example | MAPPING TBC |

The consequence is worth sitting with: collecting more species literally unlocks more of the map's materials. A narrow roster caps what you can produce no matter how well you play.

LIKE THISYou wouldn't ask a fish to chop firewood. Same rule — except here the game enforces it.

06

THE ENGINE ROOM

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — The work cycle
chunks.text:
The work cycle

Gathering runs on a repeating work-and-rest cycle that keeps going without you.

A cycle starts — you assign a Yakkamon to a resource it's allowed to gather.

It takes time — each work cycle runs for a set duration before it pays out.

It costs stamina — working burns stamina, which limits how much a monster can do in one stretch.

It produces resources — the cycle finishes and drops its haul into a storage bin.

It repeats automatically — no tapping needed. Work continues while you're off hunting or battling.

It sleeps when tired — out of stamina, the Yakkamon goes to bed, recovers, then gets back to work on its own.

WORKING→OUT OF STAMINA→SLEEPING→WORKING

A monster that's asleep isn't broken, it's recharging. There are two ways to raise output: level them up, since higher levels make them more efficient farmers, and collect more of them, since that unlocks more resource types and lets you gather several at once.

Cycle duration, stamina cost, yield per cycle and sleep recovery rate are all unpublished. Nobody can build an accurate farming calculator until they land.

LIKE THISEach monster is a little worker with a battery. Work drains it, sleep charges it, and it clocks back on without being told.

07

THE NEW SINK

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Upkeep & degradation
chunks.text:
Upkeep & degradation

Your farm wears out as you use it — a resource sink that does not exist in Sunflower Land.

Plots degrade
The job card carries a degradation marker. The example shown read degraded 1.6× — that plot farms more slowly until you refertilise it.

Fertiliser costs resources
So upkeep is a permanent drag on production rather than a cosmetic status. Bryn was clear the intent is not to punish going wide, but the cost is real.

Being away just pauses it
Degradation comes from use, not absence. Log off for a month and your Yakkamon fill the bins, then stop and wait: "no decay, no neglect feature, no punitive system for not logging in". The only cost of being away is the output you didn't bank.

Plot groups are non-linear
Growing tiles come in groups of three, and upkeep scales more slowly than production does. Filling out a group beats spreading thin — invest deep, not wide.

No numbers published. Not the degradation rate, not the fertiliser recipe, not the live group size. Only the single 1.6× example is public, and it came off a mock-up job card.

LIKE THISA vegetable patch, not a vending machine. Crop the same soil forever and yields drop until you feed it.

08

WHERE THE LOOT GOES

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Storage bins
chunks.text:
Storage bins

Gathered resources pile into a bin that keeps filling while you're gone — until it fills up and stops.

Resources don't go straight to your bag. They stack in a storage bin that keeps filling on its own, even while you're offline, until you tap it to collect the haul into your inventory.

EARLY BIN5 / 20

FILLING84 / 120

FULL — MAX120 / 120

The catch: bins have a cap. Once a bin hits MAX it stops accepting, and every hour it spends full is production you never banked. That turns bin capacity and how often you check in into a genuine strategic variable — the difference between a farm that runs all night and one that quietly stops at 2am.

LIKE THISA piggy bank that fills itself. Once it's full, extra coins bounce off the top — so empty it before it overflows.

09

UPKEEP

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Looking after them
chunks.text:
Looking after them

Your monsters have needs, and a monster that needs something isn't earning.

Status icons float above a Yakkamon when something's up, and a notification feed calls it out by name — screenshots show messages in the form of "[name] is Hungry".

Hungry
Needs feeding before it will carry on.

Hurt
Injured or knocked out, and out of action until treated.

Sleeping
Recovering stamina. Not broken — it restarts itself.

Needs an item
Can ask directly with a speech bubble, e.g. a stone icon with a "!".

Nothing gets worse while you're gone. A monster that needs something stops earning until you deal with it — that is the whole penalty. There is no hunger clock running while you're logged out.

An item bar sits along the bottom of the screen for exactly this — milk, flowers, mushrooms, a health item and more, ready to use on whoever's struggling. Because a monster in a bad state stops producing, upkeep is part of the economy rather than flavour.

LIKE THISThey're pets with jobs. Feed them, patch them up, let them nap — and they keep earning for you.

10

THE STACKING RULE

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — How boosts stack
chunks.text:
How boosts stack

A short rule with large consequences for how you build a roster.

Same name → does not stack
Two monsters both carrying "Wood Gatherer I" give you the effect once. Stacking duplicates of your best monster achieves nothing.

Different name or higher rank → stacks
"Wood Gatherer" alongside "Extreme Wood Gatherer" is two separate effects, and both apply.

What the team wants
Stated plainly: kill the reason to hoard copies, and create a strong reason to collect a broad array of monsters with different skills so you can layer boosts on one activity.

The roster shape this implies
Wide, not deep. One excellent specialist per job beats five copies of your best one — and combined with type locking, that is now the clearest planning rule available.

LIKE THISTwo identical umbrellas keep you exactly as dry as one. An umbrella and a raincoat is the upgrade.

11

THE LONG GAME

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Breeding & genetics
chunks.text:
Breeding & genetics

Where the team expects the deepest optimisation to live — on a one-to-three-year horizon.

Bloodlines carry down
Breed two strong individuals of the same species and their good stats and traits propagate, letting you aim a line at a specific result.

A breeding limit, scaled by rarity
Bred Yakkamon are tradable, so there is a cap to stop inflation: commons breed above replacement, rarer species around it, and some Legendaries may breed only once. Offspring can breed, but their own count can narrow further. Random noise still creeps in the more you breed from one individual.

80–90% predictable
One RNG component plus one fixed component, and explicitly no RNG stacked on RNG. You should be able to build a best/worst case before committing.

No forging, no evolutions at launch
Combining ten commons into one rare was rejected as tonally wrong. Evolutions are confirmed but not launching with the game — the team wants to solve the supply problem (everyone evolving up and piling at the top tier) first.

Advanced breeding is not in early access. It arrives in a chapter release after launch, alongside PvP.

LIKE THISPedigree breeding. You can keep going back to the same champion, but the litters get scruffier each time.

12

HOME

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Your base & your gym
chunks.text:
Your base & your gym

The place they all work from — and the doorway out into the wild.

Expand your land, tile by tile
Each tile carries a resource price right on the button — the starter one reads 10 Wood + 1 Stone. A tile can hold resource nodes, room for workstations and plots, or a hunting area, and every tile raises how much you can run at once.

Buildings & stations
Workbenches with their own storage counters, a workshop marked with an axe, houses with beds for sleeping monsters, crop plots and rock nodes.

Hunting Area
A dedicated zone with an entry cost shown on the sign — 5 berries in the launch screenshot. This is your doorway from farming into hunting.

The menu buttons you'll live in: Squad (your active team), Items, Quests, Shop, Trade (the player market) and Log (notification history).

LIKE THISA workshop yard. More space means more benches — and more benches mean more gets made at once.

13

THE WORLD

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — The living world
chunks.text:
The living world

A clock, weather, seasons — and a world that opens up in three layers: tiles, Regions, Chapters.

Day & night
A clock runs in the corner with a sun or moon icon, and what you find in the wild changes with it.

Weather
Separate weather indicators sit next to the clock — sunshine and rain are both shown in the HUD.

Seasons
Seasons change the world around you, and each Region shifts along with them.

Regions
Grasslands, deserts, volcanoes, fire regions and a Water Region, each with its own resources and its own monster types.

How the world expands

Tiles — your Region is made of tiles. Gather resources to unlock more (the starter one costs 10 Wood + 1 Stone). Each tile can hold fresh resources, room to build, or a hunting area — and each raises how much you can run at once.

Regions — grow your starting Region far enough and you unlock whole new ones. A Water Region has water hunting areas full of Yakkamon you could not catch back home, and its resources need the right type to gather.

Chapters — Regions get bigger each time you expand, and more arrive in upcoming Chapters alongside new species.

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — The living world
chunks.text:
Nothing you unlock ever closes. Old Regions stay part of your operation, so you end up automating and managing Yakkamon across several at once — and moving and sharing resources between Regions is, in the team’s words, "the real puzzle". That only makes sense if resources sit in the Region they were gathered in. What moving them costs is not published. Logistics between Regions →

Every three months, new monsters drop into the wild. Brand-new Yakkamon are released on a quarterly schedule and players compete to hunt them down and claim them first. Being ready when a drop lands is a real advantage — and one of the better reasons to keep your farm and gear strong between seasons.

Two caveats. The team said on 6 August that the cadence may become weekly rather than quarterly, Sunflower Land style. And day/night runs on a sped-up in-game clock, not real time — so no timezone gets a better night shift.

LIKE THISThe world has its own little day that runs faster than yours. Nobody gets a head start on sunrise.

14

GETTING STRONGER

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Hunting & crafting
chunks.text:
Hunting & crafting

Gear is how you reach the rare stuff — and the gear is built from what your ordinary monsters gathered.

Crafting
You refine gathered resources into the gear and items you need. That gear is what lets you track down and capture rarer, tougher monsters.

Hunting
Hunting is a job you assign, not a place you walk to — same top-down view as the farm. The Yakkamon you send in roams the ground while you farm, and what it meets depends on the ground, the in-game hour and the wild monster's temperament.

Grounds have areas
Three shown so far (a rocky outcrop among them), with swamps and water areas to come. Send a monster to snoop around one area to skew toward that type, or let it wander and take pot luck.

Lures and baits are crafted
A rock-type lure draws rock types. Recipes turn your gathered resources into lures and baits — and into the materials your farm needs to expand.

Aggressive encounters
A red alert on the ground means something wants to fight you. Most of the ground pauses and waits for your move — this is where hunting hands off to combat.

Ambient encounters
Skittish, they never alert you. Send your hunter over with bait, watch a short emoji conversation, and see whether it joins or runs.

Grounds deplete, monsters don't
No limit on hunts per Yakkamon. The hunting ground itself is what runs dry: the more it's hunted out, the lower its chance of producing anything.

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Hunting & crafting
chunks.text:
Contract hunts pay coins
A contract system requests specific Yakkamon and pays in coins — one of the few faucets for the currency that gates the tradable economy.

The ground has a timetable
Each ground reveals different Yakkamon at different times of day — on the sped-up in-game clock, not yours. "Learn the clock" is the team's own advice, and the table is yours to discover.

Three temperaments
Affectionate monsters come home only if your hunter wins them over. Greedy ones want resources first — bring the right goods. Angry ones start a fight a weak hunter loses.

Legendaries walk in unannounced
Legendaries and Rares sporadically appear in ordinary grounds with no schedule. Keep a strong, well-supplied team ready — and expect Seasons to change what is on the map.

The official Hunting post (5 September) is where the timetable, the temperaments and the wild Legendaries come from. Our reading of it: Every Wild Yakkamon Wants Something.

Crafting is the thing to watch, because it's what actually gates progress. Raw gathering scales easily once you have a roster; what limits most players is turning that pile into the specific items a harder hunt needs.

LIKE THISYou need a better fishing rod to catch the big fish — and you build the rod out of what the small fish helped you collect.

15

THE ARENA FLOOR

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — The battle system
chunks.text:
The battle system

Lane-based 3v3 auto-battling. Your skill shows up in the team you built, not the buttons you press.

Lane-based 3v3
Monsters hold assigned lanes and act top to bottom — lane one, then two, then three, every round. You set positions before the fight; AOE attacks keep positioning relevant.

Skills fire in a fixed order
Each monster cycles through two to three abilities in a preset order. The move list is visible in advance, which creates the core tension: type advantage versus skill-loop advantage.

You act inside the fight
Decided at the end of August: it is not a pure simulation. Players influence combat through "mechanic swapping", on an architecture built to flex once player feedback starts. What the action looks like hasn't been shown.

Who goes first
A coin flip — unless a lane holds the type advantage, which overrides everything. Fire attacking grass goes first, full stop. Lane one is where a disadvantage hurts most.

Pacing
Three to five rounds typically, under a minute. But deliberate wide variance — the "average" fight is meant to be under 40% of all fights.

Speed up, don’t skip
Battles run on an animation timer you can accelerate. Full skipping likely won’t ship, because real-time interaction mechanics are in testing.

Respeccing is expensive on purpose
The intended route is to find a monster with the skill you want and extract it onto another. Buildcraft is meant to come from breeding, not from hot-swapping loadouts before every fight.

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — The battle system
chunks.text:
Matchmaking & anti-bot
MMR confirmed. No meaningful rewards below an MMR cutoff — that is where weak human players sit, and it makes the low end worthless to bots. Better bots get flagged by event tracking.

That screenshot is a dev gym. The battle image circulating is an internal design environment with placeholder backgrounds — not the finished battle screen. Skill counts aren’t settled either; around two per monster with more passives is under consideration. Lane effects, ground types and weather are in the back pocket, not in early access.

LIKE THISYou’re a manager, not a player. Pick the squad and the formation, then watch from the touchline.

16

WHAT IT'S ALL FOR

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Arena, quests & trading
chunks.text:
Arena, quests & trading

The arena, your gym, an on-chain market, and the quests and events running alongside. For how a fight actually resolves, see the battle system.

Arena battles & your gym
You face other players in PvP arena combat and build your own gym. Since rarity and stat rolls both affect power, the team you build on the farm is the team you fight with.

Player trading, on-chain
Every core resource and creature is tradable on-chain, with a Trade button in the main menu. Two valid ways to build an empire: grind it, or trade your way there.

Two tracks: free and tradable
The free-to-play layer produces without limit but can't be traded. Making something tradable costs coins, and coins only come from VIP, burning assets or crops, and contract hunts — so the gate between the tracks is the whole economic design.

Quests & timed events
Quests appear in a feed with names like "Capture the Spikemon", and timed events run on a countdown with a milestone bar filling toward marked rewards.

PvP is not in early access. The team confirmed on 6 August that early access — November or December 2026 — ships gathering, monsters, hunting and basic combat. PvP, tournaments and advanced breeding arrive after launch in chapter releases. Guilds and alliances were pushed back further still on 21 August — explicitly behind core functionality. The full schedule →

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Arena, quests & trading
chunks.text:
LIKE THISThe farm is practice, the arena is the match — and the market is there if you'd rather buy a good player than raise one.

17

THE LONG RUN

chunks.title: How Yakkamon Works: The Full Field Guide — Progression & endgame
chunks.text:
Progression & endgame

Infinite levels, chapter releases, and a meta the team expects to move without intervening.

Infinite levels and expansions
Plans and sinks are meant to ship at launch; the endgame features themselves arrive after early access once the core has been tested.

The meta is expected to move
Early: gathering and hunting specialists are the valuable monsters, because throughput funds everything else. Later: once the arena and tournaments establish, demand shifts toward battle-stat monsters.

No hard specialisation cap
Producer versus fighter is meant to emerge from opportunity cost rather than an enforced limit. Top-end players will comfortably do both.

No resets, ever
Mistakes get worn and fixed. Inflation is attacked with hard sinks and new content that absorbs old — the pattern Sunflower Land shipped as an infinite XP sink.

Not all monsters ship at launch. Around 50–60 species open the game; new regions and species arrive per chapter, framed internally as roughly the first year of content.

LIKE THISA long-running league rather than a season that wipes. The table never resets — they just keep adding divisions.

18

Not confirmed yet

If you're planning calculators, roster planners or market tools, these are the numbers that don't exist publicly yet.

Stat systemStats vary per individual and there are hidden initial values on spawn, but the roll range, which stats exist, and how much of it is visible in game are all unknown.

Upkeep numbersThe degradation rate, the fertiliser recipe, real plot-group sizes and how steeply upkeep scales. Only the 1.6× example figure is public.

Full type chartOnly Grass→Wood is confirmed. The complete type list and the resource each unlocks is missing — and so is combat type effectiveness.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Guides: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — WHAT IS YAKKAMON?
chunks.text:
WHAT IS YAKKAMON?
▶ Prefer to watch? The 2-minute explainer ↗

Yakkamon is a creature-collector game with a twist — it's also about building something. You explore the world to hunt and catch wild monsters, then put them to work gathering resources and farming while you're off doing other things.

The world itself is alive: deserts, volcanoes, and oceans that shift between day and night, and change with the seasons. Every three months, brand-new monsters show up in the wild for players to compete to find first.

CATCH

CRAFT

EXPLORE

BUILD

BATTLE

As you play, you'll catch creatures, craft gear, and build up your own gym — grinding it out, or trading with other players, however you like.

Yakkamon comes from the team behind Sunflower Land, an established game with over a million players, so it's being built by people with years of experience running a live game. See all the gameplay systems →

chunks.title: Yakkamon Deposit Leaderboard: Base + Ronin Points — WHAT EACH BAND TAKES

WHAT EACH BAND TAKES

The airdrop pays by band, not by a sliding scale. Everyone who finishes between 51st and 250th takes home the same Echo; 50th takes a Storm; 5,001st takes nothing at all. Points spent inside a band you have already cleared buy you nothing — only crossing into the next one does.

These lines move every time someone deposits, and they only account for deposit points. The leaderboard that decides the airdrop locks one week before early access — holding a band matters as much as reaching it, because there is no partial credit for finishing 5,001st.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Deposit Leaderboard: Base + Ronin Points — HOW THE POINTS ARE WORKED OUT
chunks.text:
HOW THE POINTS ARE WORKED OUT

THE FORMULA

points = amount × (week multiplier + bulk bonus)

The two bonuses add together, they do not multiply. At 2.8×, a 500 $FLOWER deposit earns 1,400 points plus a 100 bonus — the bonus is 20% of the deposit, not 20% of the points.

The bulk bonus is rated on each transfer on its own: +10% at 50, +20% at 500, +40% at 5,000, +80% at 50,000. Splitting one deposit into several can drop each piece into a lower band. The week multiplier starts at 3.0× and falls 0.2× a week to a 1.0× floor — held at 2.8× for week 3 after the week-2 deposit pause — with windows turning at 02:00 UTC.

Deposits made on both chains are added together, because one deposit address covers Base and Ronin alike. Everything here is read from public blockchain data and recalculated regularly.

chunks.text:
1. GETTING STARTED

Not registered yet?

It takes about a minute and needs only an email address. Registering through our link applies access code YAKKA-UDBVPX, which gets you a Gold Box in game.

SIGN UP FREE ↗

▶ Prefer to watch? How to pre-register, in 3 minutes ↗
Sign up with just an email to claim a Monster Egg — and nothing else. From there, you earn points by staying active before launch — the more points you earn, the better your rewards when the game opens.

🥚

— trainers registered

As of — · last known figure, not live · official site ↗

Your points decide three things:

Your trainer number — your permanent rank among the founding players.

Which wave you join — higher-ranked players get in first when early access opens.

What you receive at launch — including a shot at a free Genesis monster (see below).

How to earn points:

Tap your egg once a day (bonus points for keeping a daily streak going)

Link your Discord and Twitter, and post weekly

Refer friends — you earn points for every signup

Take part in the free mint (see below) — 250 points

Deposit $FLOWER early (see below)

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 2. IMPORTANT DATES
chunks.text:
The leaderboard finalises one week before early access launch. The rank you hold at that moment is the rank your rewards are calculated on — points earned after it cannot change your tier, your monster, or your wave. The team has said the exact date will be announced with plenty of notice beforehand.

What this means for you:

Deposit sooner rather than later. The points multiplier on $FLOWER deposits is at its highest right now and steps down every week, so the same deposit is worth less the longer you leave it.

Climb before the lock. Everything that decides your reward — your monster, your wave, your trainer number — is settled the moment the leaderboard finalises.

Rewards land three days later. Your airdrop arrives shortly after the lock, ahead of launch day.

Utilities are out. The official Yakkapedia now names what each Genesis Legendary does — as descriptive text, with the numbers still being balanced — so you know what you're climbing toward. The table →

10 September is the mint deadline, not the 14th. The free mint whitelists are taken from the leaderboard on 10 September. Your rank that day — and whether you have 5 $FLOWER deposited — decides which waves you can mint in.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 2. IMPORTANT DATES
chunks.text:
Wave 4 is the one gap. Waves 1 to 3 enter a week apart, but Wave 4 — ranks 20,001 to 100,000, most of everyone who gets in at all — is only "confirmed closer to launch". Deposited $FLOWER unlocks when you get access, not on launch day, so if you've deposited, the top-20,000 line is worth more than the reward ladder alone suggests. Our full read on the schedule →

Dates firm up as we get closer. Timings here are the team's current plan, and anything without a fixed date will be confirmed and announced in advance. We track this page against the official docs and update it when they move.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 3. REWARD TRACK
chunks.text:
3. REWARD TRACK

▶ The reward track explained →
The reward track runs on a weekly cycle, not on fixed points milestones. Every 7 days, a fresh list of rewards appears for you to claim.

Claimed items go straight into your inventory and stay there.

Once you have early access, you'll be able to claim them inside the game.

Each new list replaces the last one — so anything you don't claim is gone.

Check back every 7 days. Because each list replaces the previous one, logging in weekly is the only way to keep collecting.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 4. MONSTER EGG TIERS
chunks.text:
4. MONSTER EGG TIERS

Sign-up order decides exactly one thing: which Monster Egg you start with. Tiers are handed out in registration order, and once a tier is full, it's gone.

Sign-up position | Monster Egg |

1 – 10,000 | 💎 Platinum |

10,001 – 25,000 | 🥇 Gold |

25,001 – 50,000 | 🥈 Silver |

50,001 – 100,000 | 🥉 Bronze |

100,001 – 500,000 | Basic |

Your Monster Egg is not an NFT. It's an in-game item — nothing to mint, nothing to claim, no wallet needed. It simply appears on your farm the first time you log into Yakkamon.

Sign-up egg tiers are mainly cosmetic. The team has confirmed the tiers function as cosmetic and early-collectible differences rather than as power. Every monster works as a worker for you whichever egg it came from — so a Platinum egg is not a head start on the leaderboard and carries no claim on early access.

Signed up late? You can still finish at the top. A Basic egg holder who earns points daily will finish above a Platinum egg holder who signs up and never comes back. Rank is earned, not reserved.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 5. REFERRAL RULES
chunks.text:
5. REFERRAL RULES

▶ The new referral rules, and what they cost →
Referrals earn points, but only genuine ones count. Referrals are reviewed before rewards are finalized, and points from them stay provisional until that review.

A referral only counts if the friend is a real, separate person with a verified account who actually engages with pre-registration. Each counting referral is worth 75 points, and referrals are uncapped. Your first five are instant — they pay the moment your friend signs up. From the sixth onward, your friend must link a wallet and deposit 100 $FLOWER of their own before the points land. Linking Discord and X no longer verifies a referral: bot accounts were clearing that bar in bulk. These do not count:

Referrals past your fifth are no longer free. The bar is now a 100 $FLOWER deposit made by your friend, with their own money and their own wallet — not something you can complete on their behalf, and not something a genuinely free-to-play friend will clear. What this costs, and who it hits →

Unverified accounts — sign-ups that never complete verification.

Multi-accounting — referring yourself via alt accounts, throwaway emails, or shared devices and wallets.

Bots and automation — bulk or scripted sign-ups.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 5. REFERRAL RULES
chunks.text:
Referrals 6+ where the friend hasn't deposited — from your sixth referral on, the friend must link a wallet and deposit 100 $FLOWER themselves. Their deposit also earns them points, so it isn't purely a cost to them — but it is real money. Why this changed →

Inactive sign-ups — accounts created purely to farm a referral bonus, with no real activity.

Removed referrals are deducted from your total, which can lower your trainer number and your tier. Serious or repeated abuse can disqualify an account from pre-registration rewards entirely.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 6. GENESIS MONSTERS
chunks.text:
6. GENESIS MONSTERS

▶ The full airdrop write-up →
When early access opens, the 5,000 highest-ranked players each get a free Genesis Monster — a powerful starter creature that will never be available again to anyone, at any price. The top 2,000 get an even rarer Legendary version.

Genuinely powerful — not just a collectible. It's a real head start in the game.

Starts with XP — it arrives already leveled up, ahead of monsters caught on day one.

Fully yours — you can trade it with other players if you want to.

Specialized — some are built for battle, some for gathering resources, some for other parts of the game.

This is not first come, first served. Monster NFTs are awarded on points, not on how early you signed up. Signing up does not reserve one — you have to earn your rank and hold it until the leaderboard locks.

There is no sale. No second window. No way to buy in later. The only route is to finish pre-registration inside the top 5,000 on points. Once the leaderboard locks, this airdrop is closed for good.

Who gets an airdrop

Leaderboard rank (by points) | Airdrop |

1 – 2,000 | Genesis Legendary Monster NFT |

2,001 – 5,000 | Rare Egg |

5,001+ | Not eligible for the airdrop |

Late to pre-registration? You are not locked out. The leaderboard is points-based, so a trainer who signs up today and grinds daily can pass someone who signed up on day one and stopped showing up.

Which early-access wave you enter

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 6. GENESIS MONSTERS
chunks.text:
The Trainer Point airdrop is a one-time chance to own some of the most powerful monsters in the game — and it grants early access too. Your place is your leaderboard rank at the moment of the airdrop, earned on points, so it's still there to be climbed.

Points rank | Genesis Legendary |

1 – 3 | 🌩 Storm + ⬜ Echo |

4 – 10 | 🌩 Storm + 👻 Ghost |

11 – 50 | 🌩 Storm |

51 – 250 | ⬜ Echo |

251 – 500 | 👻 Ghost |

501 – 2,000 | 🌸 Bloom |

2,001 – 5,000 | Rare Egg |

5,001+ | ❌ Not eligible |

The top 2,000 trainers each receive one of the four Genesis Legendaries — the founding set, earned on the leaderboard alone. Ranks 2,001–5,000 receive a Rare Egg.

Storm is the newest monster and the hardest to earn. It sits above everything else, and the only way to be airdropped one is to finish in the top 50. The top 10 receive Storm and a second Genesis Legendary alongside it.

You have to hold your rank, not just reach it. The airdrop settles when the leaderboard locks, and once it does it’s closed for good. Sitting inside the top 2,000 today guarantees nothing if others pass you before then. The lock lands one week before early access launch — see important dates — but the exact day is still to be announced.

Twice as many Legendaries as before. Legendary monsters used to stop at rank 1,000. They now run all the way to rank 2,000.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 6. GENESIS MONSTERS
chunks.text:
Updated 2 September — two names changed, and the utilities are out. The official Yakkapedia now lists the four as Storm, Echo, Ghost and Bloom: the 251–500 monster previously called Bloom is now Ghost, and the 501–2,000 monster previously called Tide is now Bloom. Same monsters, same boosts, renamed to match their types. Their utilities: Storm makes Yakkamon within range work 2× as fast (large AOE), Echo doubles the resources of those within range (small AOE), Ghost keeps those within range at maximum stamina (small AOE), and Bloom regenerates a share of its Max HP every combat turn. Supplies are 75 / 275 / 400 / 2,000. The full table →

Early access waves

Separately from the eggs, your rank decides which wave you enter the game in. The 12 August update covered reward eggs only and didn’t restate the wave bands, so these are as previously published:

Points rank | Early access |

1 – 1,000 | Wave 1 |

1,001 – 5,000 | Wave 2 |

5,001 – 20,000 | Wave 3 |

20,001 – 100,000 | Wave 4 |

100,001+ | ❌ No early access |

Echo, Ghost and Bloom are different roles, not three rungs. Echo and Ghost are farm auras (double output; never tired) and Bloom is a combat passive (HP regeneration every turn). Storm is the one the team places above the rest. Landing at rank 700 gets you a different monster, not a weaker one — and the scarcity runs the other way from the ladder: 2,000 Bloom exist against 400 Ghost and 275 Echo. More on this →

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 6. GENESIS MONSTERS
chunks.text:
Only the top 100,000 trainers get early access. Pre-registering does not qualify you on its own — you have to finish inside the top 100,000 on points. Below that, you wait for full launch.

The egg counter on the sign-up page is unrelated to this airdrop. That counter tracks Monster Egg tiers only. It is not counting down Monster NFTs and it has nothing to do with your leaderboard rank.

You won't know which individual you got until launch. A live "Reveal Event" unwraps every Genesis monster at once — though since the Yakkapedia, you do know which species and utility each rank band is in line for.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 7. FREE MINT — 14 SEPTEMBER
chunks.text:
7. FREE MINT — 14 SEPTEMBER

Updated 2 September from the official free mint page and the free-mint dev stream. Previously mid-September; before that October 1st.

▶ The Ultimate Ronin Free Mint Guide — waves, checklist, mint day →
▶ Every decision from the free-mint stream, graded →
On 14 September a free mint of 10,000 hidden Genesis monster NFTs opens on the Ronin Launchpad. It runs in five whitelisted waves over five days, each open to a different slice of the leaderboard, and it costs nothing beyond the network fee (gas, paid in RON). Your leaderboard rank on 10 September decides which waves you are on the list for.

When | 14 September, then one wave a day to 18 September |

Where | Ronin Launchpad — on the Ronin blockchain, the network Yakkamon runs on |

Cost | Free — you only pay gas, in RON |

Supply | 10,000 — 68 Legendaries (3 Storm, 5 Echo, 10 Ghost, 50 Bloom), 50 Rares and 9,882 Uncommons |

Who | Whitelisted trainers, by leaderboard rank at the 10 September snapshot — see the waves below |

How many | One NFT per wave per account; you can mint in every wave you qualify for |

Reveal | 14 October — all 10,000 revealed at once |

The five waves

Wave | Date | Supply | Who can mint |

Wave 1 | 14 Sept | 1,000 | Top 1,000 leaderboard trainers — guaranteed, mint at your own pace |

Wave 2 | 15 Sept | 3,000 | Ranks 1–10,000, with a 5 $FLOWER minimum deposit |

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 7. FREE MINT — 14 SEPTEMBER
chunks.text:
Wave 3 (Ronin wave) | 16 Sept | 2,000 | Active Ronin gamers on a list the Ronin team is building from other Ronin games — not the Yakkamon leaderboard |

Wave 4 | 17 Sept | 5,000 | Ranks 1–20,000, with a 5 $FLOWER minimum deposit — ends early if the 10,000 sell out |

Ecosystem airdrop | TBD | 1,500 | Sent manually: 1,000 to top Ronin spenders, 500 to $FLOWER ecosystem players. Likely a week after the mint, before the reveal |

The wave supplies add up to 11,000 against a 10,000 collection — later waves only get what earlier waves left. The dates after Wave 1 are the team’s current plan and were described as tentative on the stream, pending feedback on time zones and durations.

Minting earns 250 points — more than three referrals for one click, and it lands on your leaderboard score ahead of the final lock.

Get to the rank you want by 10 September. Whitelists are finalised from the leaderboard inside yakkamon.com that day. After that, climbing changes nothing for the mint.

Deposit at least 5 $FLOWER if you are counting on Wave 2 or Wave 4. It is fully withdrawable — it exists to make multi-accounting expensive, at the Ronin team’s suggestion — and more than 3,000 of the top 10,000 already qualify.

Have a Ronin wallet connected and some RON in it for gas. Base deposits count for points, but the mint is Ronin only.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 7. FREE MINT — 14 SEPTEMBER
chunks.text:
Be online when your wave opens. Outside the guaranteed top-1,000 wave, it is fastest-click: "there is usually more people than that supply", in Adam’s words, and not everyone gets one.

Mint in every wave you qualify for. One per wave per account, so a top-1,000 trainer with a 5 $FLOWER deposit can mint in Waves 1, 2, 4 and 5.

You mint blind. All 10,000 stay sealed until 14 October, when every one is revealed at once. That is before the leaderboard finalises, so you’ll know what you’re holding while you can still climb. Hidden NFTs are tradable before the reveal as well as after — and this collection is the ongoing Yakkamon collection, so new monsters released later appear in it too.

What changed from the earlier plan. The mint used to be described as a verified whitelist with one mint per trainer and no race. It is now rank-gated waves with a set supply per wave, one mint per wave per account, and speed matters in every wave except the first. The 5-Legendary figure from the old docs is gone too: 68 Legendaries are hidden in the pool. Our grades for each of those decisions →

After the reveal, you deposit them into the game. A few weeks after 14 October, or whenever you get access, minted monsters can be deposited into Yakkamon and played. The free mint and the Genesis airdrop are separate things: the airdrop is on final rank and lands automatically, the mint is something you do yourself in your wave.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Early Access Guide: Pre-Registration, Points & Free Mint — 8. FLOWER DEPOSITS
chunks.text:
8. FLOWER DEPOSITS

▶ The official deposit guideline, explained →
$FLOWER is the in-game currency already used across the studio's other games — Yakkamon doesn't launch a new one. Depositing early is like pre-loading credit before the store opens.

Every deposit does two things at once:

Saves it for you — it's held and ready the moment you get game access.

Earns points now — open now (since Aug 9, 8:00 PM ET), minimum 5 $FLOWER, sent on Base or Ronin. Points are boosted two ways: a weekly multiplier of 3× in the opening week, falling 0.2× each week to a floor of 1× (week 3 held at 2.8× after the week-2 pause), and a size bonus rated per deposit doubling from +10% at 50 $FLOWER to +80% at 50,000. Both favor depositing early, in one transfer. The full schedule →

You're not trading one for the other — you keep the $FLOWER and the points.

Where to get it — $FLOWER is the same ERC20 token on Base and Ronin, at one identical contract address, so neither chain needs bridging. You can earn it free by playing Sunflower Land, or buy it — through a swap on Base, or directly inside the Ronin Wallet. The official deposits page now publishes the contract address and the buy links; verify against it before you swap. Where to get $FLOWER →

Once you're in the game, you can spend it on gear and crafting, or withdraw it with no tax, any time.

chunks.text: For security, small percentage-based withdrawal limits may apply during the first few weeks after launch. This only limits how much you can withdraw at once while things stabilise — not whether you can withdraw at all.
