chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 1. DEPOSIT $FLOWER EARLY, AND IN SINGLE LARGER TRANSFERS
chunks.text:
1. DEPOSIT $FLOWER EARLY, AND IN SINGLE LARGER TRANSFERS

▶ Read this tip as an article →

Updated 7 August 2026 — this tip previously said the opposite. Until the first dev stream, the bonus appeared to follow your cumulative deposited total, which made splitting deposits across weeks free. The team has since described a different structure: a weekly multiplier that decays, and a size bonus applied per deposit. Both reward depositing early and in bigger single transfers. We've rewritten this tip rather than quietly editing it. What changed →

If you plan to deposit $FLOWER, when you send it and how many transfers you split it into both change how many points you get. Two separate bonuses are in play, and they push in the same direction.

Bonus one: the weekly multiplier decays

Every $FLOWER earns points, and the rate depends on which week you deposit in. The opening week pays 3×, and the rate falls by 0.2× every week until it settles at 1× and stops dropping.

Week | Dates | Rate |

1 | 10 – 16 Aug | 3.0× |

2 | 17 – 23 Aug | 2.8× |

3 | 24 – 30 Aug | 2.8× — held |

4 | 31 Aug – 6 Sep | 2.6× |

5 | 7 – 13 Sep | 2.4× |

6 | 14 – 20 Sep | 2.2× |

7 | 21 – 27 Sep | 2.0× |

8 | 28 Sep – 4 Oct | 1.8× |

9 | 5 – 11 Oct | 1.6× |

10 | 12 – 18 Oct | 1.4× |

11 | 19 – 25 Oct | 1.2× |

12+ | 26 Oct onward | 1.0× — the floor |

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 1. DEPOSIT $FLOWER EARLY, AND IN SINGLE LARGER TRANSFERS
chunks.text:
Updated 24 August — week 3 stays at 2.8×. Depositing was paused during week 2, so rather than dropping to 2.6×, the team held the week 3 multiplier at 2.8×. The 0.2× weekly step resumes from week 4, which pushes every later week — and the 1.0× floor — one week later than originally scheduled.

On the second dev stream the team acknowledged deposits may close while the multiplier is still around 1.2×, so the 1.0× floor may never actually be reached. What else changed →

The rates are official — including the week-3 hold at 2.8×. The week boundaries are our own calculation from the 10 Aug opening, so check the deposit panel if a date is borderline for you.

The multiplier applies to points, not your balance. You still hold the same $FLOWER and can withdraw or spend it in-game once access opens.

Bonus two: the size bonus is per deposit

On top of the multiplier, larger deposits earn bonus points. The rate doubles at every step, up to +80% at 50,000 $FLOWER — and it's calculated on the size of a single transfer, not on your running total.

Single deposit | Bonus rate | Points in the opening week |

50 $FLOWER | +10% | 150 +5 bonus |

500 $FLOWER | +20% | 1,500 +100 bonus |

5,000 $FLOWER | +40% | 15,000 +2,000 bonus |

50,000 $FLOWER | +80% | 150,000 +40,000 bonus |

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 1. DEPOSIT $FLOWER EARLY, AND IN SINGLE LARGER TRANSFERS
chunks.text:
The full amount must land in one go. Split deposits each earn their own smaller bonus — so 25 $FLOWER followed by another 25 does not reach the 50 tier, and ten deposits of 500 earn ten 20% bonuses instead of one 40% bonus.

What waiting costs you

Same 5,000 $FLOWER, one transfer, different weeks:

Deposited in | Total points | Versus week one |

Week 1 (3.0×) | 17,000 | — |

Week 3 (2.8×) | 16,000 | −1,000 |

Week 6 (2.2×) | 13,000 | −4,000 |

Week 12 (1.0×) | 7,000 | −10,000 |

What splitting costs you

Same 5,000 $FLOWER, all inside the opening week:

How you send it | Total points | Lost |

One transfer of 5,000 | 17,000 | — |

Ten transfers of 500 | 16,000 | −1,000 |

A hundred transfers of 50 | 15,500 | −1,500 |

Both mistakes together. Ten deposits of 500 made after the multiplier bottoms out earn 6,000 points — against 17,000 for a single 5,000 transfer in the opening week. That's a 65% loss on identical money.

What that means in practice

Deposit in the opening week if you can. 3× is the highest rate there will ever be, and it falls 0.2× every week after.

Send it in one transfer rather than several, so the size bonus lands on the full amount.

Don't hold back for a big finish. The old instinct — wait, watch the leaderboard, deposit at the end to secure a rank — is exactly what this structure is designed to punish.

Minimum deposit is 5 $FLOWER, on Base or Ronin.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 1. DEPOSIT $FLOWER EARLY, AND IN SINGLE LARGER TRANSFERS
chunks.text:
Points land in the week your deposit confirms, so send early in a week rather than at the boundary.

One thing that hasn't changed

The leaderboard is still two competitions, and that's still worth playing for:

| Final ranking | Weekly ranking |

Based on | Your total points, all-time | Points you earned that week |

Resets | Never — it accumulates | Every week |

Pays out | Once, at early access in Nov / Dec 2026 | Every single week until then |

Rewards | Legendary / Rare reward egg, early-access wave | Resource box, food box, raffle ticket, loot box |

The difference is that deposits are no longer the way to play the weekly board. Nurture, quests, referrals and X posts all feed your weekly total, and they're spread across the whole window by nature. Log in weekly and claim your boxes — just don't hold $FLOWER back to do it.

Check it against your own dashboard. The rates above come from the official deposit panel, and the maths checks out — but the week boundaries are our calculation, and the team is still tuning things. Confirm in your own deposit panel before sending, particularly if you're close to a week edge.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 2. NURTURE AFTER 12:00 UTC, EVERY DAY
chunks.text:
2. NURTURE AFTER 12:00 UTC, EVERY DAY

▶ Read this tip as an article →
Daily nurture is the main points lever for anyone not depositing, and it pays more the longer your run goes. There's also a grace period built into it — but the grace period only actually protects you if you nurture in the second half of the UTC day. That's the whole tip, and the reason is a quirk of how two separate clocks interact.

What a streak is worth

Tap your egg three times to nurture it, once a day. Each nurture pays 5 points plus a streak bonus that climbs with the run:

Streak day | Points per day |

Day 1 – 2 | +6 |

Day 3 – 4 | +7 |

Day 5 – 9 | +8 |

Day 10 – 29 | +9 |

Day 30+ | +10 |

A full week at day 30+ is 70 points. Run it unbroken from early August to the free mint in mid-September — about 42 days — and daily nurture alone is worth about 526 points.

What breaking it costs

Miss the window and your next nurture starts again at day 1. You don't just lose one day — you drop from 10 points a day back to 6, and it takes 29 days to climb back to the top rate. That rebuild is 44 points you'd have banked by staying on the ladder, on top of the day you missed.

Over 57 days | Points from nurture |

Never broken | 526 |

Broken once | ~474 |

Broken four times | ~420 |

The two clocks

Two rules govern the streak, and they don't line up:

One nurture per day, and the day rolls over at midnight UTC.

You always have 36 hours from your last nurture before the run resets.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 2. NURTURE AFTER 12:00 UTC, EVERY DAY
chunks.text:
36 hours is a day and a half, which is where the "a single missed day need not cost you the streak" promise comes from. But whether it actually covers a missed day depends entirely on when in the UTC day you tapped.

DAY 1 (UTC)
DAY 2
DAY 3

NURTURE 08:00 UTC

36-HOUR WINDOW

Window dies inside Day 2 — you must nurture tomorrow or the run resets.

NURTURE 20:00 UTC

36-HOUR WINDOW

Window reaches into Day 3 — skip Day 2 entirely and the streak survives.

Same 36 hours, different protection. Nurture before noon UTC and the grace period expires before the next day is over; nurture after noon and it carries you past it.

Why noon UTC is the line

Nurture at time T and your deadline is T plus 36 hours. For that deadline to land past the end of the next day, T has to be at least 12:00 UTC. Tap at 08:00 and your window closes at 20:00 the following day — you're still on the hook tomorrow. Tap at 20:00 and it closes at 08:00 the day after — you can miss a whole day and be fine.

12:00 UTC is… | Local time |

Los Angeles | 5:00 AM |

New York | 8:00 AM |

São Paulo | 9:00 AM |

London | 1:00 PM |

Berlin | 2:00 PM |

Istanbul | 3:00 PM |

Mumbai | 5:30 PM |

Manila | 8:00 PM |

Tokyo | 9:00 PM |

Sydney | 10:00 PM |

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 2. NURTURE AFTER 12:00 UTC, EVERY DAY
chunks.text:
The practical version. In the Americas almost any waking-hours nurture already clears noon UTC, so you're fine by default. In Europe, Asia and Australia it's the opposite — a morning nurture is before the cutoff and leaves you no slack at all. If you're east of London, make it an evening habit.

Practical notes

Nurturing late one day and early the next is fine — they're different UTC days, so both count and the run continues.

The 36-hour grace is a safety net, not a schedule. Using it every other day means you're nurturing half as often and earning half as many points.

Nurture points feed your weekly total as well as your all-time one, so a consistent run helps in both competitions at once.

Set a repeating alarm for the same time each evening. That single habit is worth more than any other free action on the board.

Be realistic about scale: 526 points over 57 days is a fraction of what a large $FLOWER deposit pays. It's the best free lever there is, not a way to out-earn capital.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 3. YOUR DEPOSIT IS ALSO YOUR LAUNCH WAR-CHEST
chunks.text:
3. YOUR DEPOSIT IS ALSO YOUR LAUNCH WAR-CHEST

▶ Read this tip as an article →
Most people deposit $FLOWER for the points. The official deposit page now describes a second return on the same money: a run of early-access-only offers that can only be bought with a balance that is already in the game when the doors open. Depositing now earns the points and books your seat for those.

What the docs say your balance buys at launch

Offer | What the docs say | When |

Discounted Gems | "Gems at early access rates — the best pricing we’ll offer" | Early access |

VIP access | Unlock VIP status and its perks | Early access |

Exclusive items | Launch-window gear, cosmetics and collectibles "you won’t be able to pick up later" | Early access |

Auctions | Bid $FLOWER on rare and one-off items | Chapter 0 (one month after early access) |

The in-game economy | Crafting materials, hunting supplies, gear | From early access |

Source: the official $FLOWER Deposits page. Prices and quantities are unpublished; the docs call the offers "time-limited and, in the case of auctions and exclusive items, limited in supply too", and say more will be announced before early access.

The line that matters, in the team’s words: "Trainers who arrive with $FLOWER ready are the ones who get first pick." A balance you deposit in September is sitting in the game on launch day. One you meant to top up in December is competing with everyone else’s deposit at 1.0× — if deposits are still open at all.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 3. YOUR DEPOSIT IS ALSO YOUR LAUNCH WAR-CHEST
chunks.text:
What this changes about how you deposit

Don’t size your deposit on points alone. The same $FLOWER pays twice: leaderboard points now, first pick of the launch offers later. If you were going to buy Gems or VIP anyway, the $FLOWER for that is better deposited now at 2.6× than held back.

Don’t plan to pull it straight back out. Withdrawals open at Chapter 0, a month after early access — December or January at the earliest — and the docs warn of percentage-based withdrawal limits in the first weeks. Money you need this year should not go in.

Keep some of the balance unspent for Chapter 0. Auctions are the one offer that is both time- and supply-limited and arrives a month after everything else. A trainer who spends the whole balance on day one has nothing to bid.

Early access wave still gates all of this. The offers are available to trainers who are in the game. Wave 4 has no confirmed date, so a rank inside the top 20,000 (Wave 3) is worth more than the offers table suggests.

Our reading, not the docs’. The official page lists the offers and says they are limited; it does not say what they cost or how many there are. Treat "first pick" as the promise, and the rest of this tip as the obvious consequence of it. We will update the table when prices land.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 4. DEPOSIT ON RONIN IF YOU HAVEN’T YET
chunks.text:
4. DEPOSIT ON RONIN IF YOU HAVEN’T YET

▶ Read this tip as an article →
$FLOWER is the same token at the same contract address on Base and Ronin, and a deposit earns identical points on either chain. Until now the choice didn’t matter. It does now, for one reason: the free mint on 14 September happens only on Ronin, and gas for it is paid in RON. If you have not deposited yet, doing it on Ronin means the wallet, the swap and the RON are all in place before mint day, instead of being a separate job the week it matters.

Why Ronin, if the points are the same

| Deposit on Base | Deposit on Ronin |

Points | Identical | Identical |

Counts for the 5 $FLOWER mint condition | Yes | Yes |

Can that wallet mint? | No — the mint is Ronin only | Yes, once linked |

Gas token for the mint | Still need RON in a Ronin wallet | RON, already in the wallet you used |

Where to buy $FLOWER | Uniswap (USDC pair) | The swap inside Ronin Wallet |

Contract address on both chains: 0x3E12b9d6A4D12cd9b4a6d613872d0Eb32f68b380. Check it against the official deposits page before you swap — a copycat FLOWER pair exists on Base.

How to do it

Install the official Ronin Wallet (browser extension or mobile), write the recovery phrase down offline, and fund it with a little RON — bought inside the wallet or withdrawn from an exchange that supports Ronin.

chunks.title: Yakkamon Trainer Tips: Deposit Timing, Nurture Tactics & the Mint — 4. DEPOSIT ON RONIN IF YOU HAVEN’T YET
chunks.text:
Swap for $FLOWER inside Ronin Wallet, then send it to your own deposit address from the yakkamon.com deposit panel. Minimum 5 $FLOWER; one transfer rather than several, for the size bonus.

Link that Ronin wallet to your Yakkamon account before the 10 September snapshot. The whitelist is checked against the wallet, so the one that mints must be the one that is linked.

Leave the RON in it. That is your mint-day gas. Only Wave 5 has a published time (00:00 UTC on the 18th), so don’t plan to buy RON at wave open.

Already deposited on Base?

Nothing to undo. Your points are safe, the 5 $FLOWER condition is met on either chain, and there is no need to bridge anything — your deposit address accepts both chains, and the mint doesn’t care where your $FLOWER sits. You just need a Ronin wallet as well: set one up, fund it with RON, link it to your account, and mint from that. Any further deposits are simpler from Ronin, for the same reasons above.

Two things this tip is not saying. It is not saying Base deposits are worth less — they aren’t. And it is not saying to move existing $FLOWER between chains — that costs fees and changes nothing. It is only saying that the next deposit you make is easier on the chain you will be minting on anyway.

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: overview
chunks.text:
# Yakkamon — current state of the game

Current as of the 1 September 2026 stream · digest version 2026-09-02 · four streams merged

Every statement carries the date of the stream it came from, e.g. 01 Sep. Where a later stream changed or contradicted an earlier one, the later stream wins: the current position is stated in the topic section and the old position is logged in section 17 ("Superseded"). Only the four transcripts above were used; nothing here comes from other sources. The team's standing disclaimer applies to everything: the game is in development and anything discussed can change before launch.

Sources, oldest → newest

- 6 Aug 2026 — First official stream · trainer dashboard, deposits, design pillars

- 13 Aug 2026 — Airdrop rework, OG title, tradability, timeline

- 21 Aug 2026 — Biome pack, combat system, upkeep UI, audio

- 1 Sep 2026 — Ronin free mint waves, Yakopedia, economy model, hunting

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 1. Key dates and timeline
chunks.text:

| When | What | Source |

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 2. Studio and team
chunks.text:
## 2. Studio and team

- Yakkamon is the second major IP from the Sunflower Land team (Thought Farmer Studio). It is a separate project from Sunflower Land but reuses the FLOWER token, may have light lore crossovers, and shares the same retro/bright art family while having its own look, monsters, backgrounds and HD UI. 06 Aug

- Communities are deliberately separated: Sunflower Land questions go to the Sunflower Land streams, Yakkamon streams are Yakkamon-only. 06 Aug

- Adam — hosts the streams (Craig's "fearless leader"); works on infrastructure (login, news, referral systems, Discord integration into the game), UI modals and battle prototyping. 06 Aug, 13 Aug, 21 Aug, 01 Sep

- Bryn — lead game designer, owns the systems design; splits time with Sunflower Land in waves (roughly 50/50 on average). Online handle "Jam Boy Magic". 06 Aug, 13 Aug, 01 Sep

- Spencer — main engineer, ~90% on Yakkamon; building the UI, world, expansions, hunting grounds, crafting, login flow and buildings, and generating the AI-drafted animations; self-described perfectionist who sets the polish standard. 06 Aug, 13 Aug, 21 Aug, 01 Sep

- Craig — "mastermind" of the trainer dashboard; joined the Yakkamon game build the week of 13 Aug; owns deposits, free-mint contracts and AI-generated audio, and presented the animation drafts (plus his own A-Rock "Harry Potter portrait" test). 06 Aug, 13 Aug, 21 Aug, 01 Sep

- Elias — was mainly on Sunflower Land 06 Aug; present on the 1 Sep stream.

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 2. Studio and team
chunks.text:
- Matt L — 12-week game design intern from Bryn's old university; focused on combat and skill design and credited with a large share of the battle system. 06 Aug, 21 Aug

- Gabby — lead artist; Yakkamon monsters are designed in-house by Gabby's art team. 13 Aug, 21 Aug

- Daniel Diggle — external artist behind the original Sunnyside/Sunflower Land asset pack; designed the new Yakkamon UI and HUD (finished by 21 Aug) and gave the team early, exclusive access to a brand-new biome pack (biomes, seasons, elements). 06 Aug, 21 Aug

- Ronin team (incl. Jiho) — guiding the launchpad process, supplying extra whitelist lists, reviewing the mint contracts. 01 Sep

- Community language: players are "trainers"; Adam gets called "Professor Oak"; sign-offs in play include "Yakadabadoo", "Yakka jam", "Get hype". 06 Aug, 21 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 3. Pre-registration, trainer dashboard and points
chunks.text:
## 3. Pre-registration, trainer dashboard and points

Numbers - Pre-registered trainers: 45,000 06 Aug → 100,000 21 Aug. - About 10,000 came in through private trainer codes distributed via Sunflower Land (and a small number via Ronin); another 8–9,000 tried to sign up without a code before referrals opened; referrals then "went crazy". 06 Aug - 4,500–5,000 bot accounts were banned; referrals will be double-verified before the leaderboard is finalised. 06 Aug

X / Twitter - The original "Play Yakamon" X account was compromised and a phishing link was posted. The team created a new official X account rather than wait on X support. 06 Aug - Trainer dashboard lets you connect to the new account: +10 points. Anyone who connected the old account keeps those points, so they can hold 20 points from X in total. Reconnect shows in the dashboard if you previously connected. 06 Aug - Nothing in the game itself was compromised; no need to re-register. Three or four fake websites were taken down. The official site is yakkamon.com — always check official links. 06 Aug

Wallets - Wallet linking is live in the dashboard. 06 Aug - Option to change a linked wallet is being looked into; no ETA. 13 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 3. Pre-registration, trainer dashboard and points
chunks.text:
Discord points - A Discord emoji-reward feature (mods and players handing out emojis) hit ~10 messages/second and turned into reaction farming, so it was switched off. A manual weekly reward system was floated. 06 Aug - "We're not doing Discord points anymore" — memes earn personal appreciation only. 13 Aug - Bot sign-up waves also triggered a 3-day Discord restriction on the server (no image posting, invite links broken); the team is now stricter on verification to protect the game, economy and server. 13 Aug - Discord is being integrated into the game: Discord updates and communication will appear in-game, plus a light role system between the two. 21 Aug

### Early FLOWER deposit

- Went live 10 Aug (delayed from 5 Aug). Rules are on the website. 06 Aug

- Deposited FLOWER stays yours — you can withdraw it or spend it in-game later. Deposits are not a purchase. 06 Aug, 13 Aug

- Bonus 1 — weekly multiplier: week 1 pays points equal to 3× the FLOWER deposited (5 FLOWER → 15 points). The multiplier drops by 0.2× each week; with the leaderboard's likely timing it "may never reach 1" and could end around 1.2× when deposits close. If it does reach 1× it stays at 1× — it will not go below. 06 Aug, 13 Aug

- Bonus 2 — size bonus, per single deposit: 50 FLOWER → +5 bonus points, 500 FLOWER → +100 bonus points, scaling with deposit size. Must be one transaction (two 25s do not equal one 50). 06 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 3. Pre-registration, trainer dashboard and points
chunks.text:
- Design intent: reward depositing early rather than a last-minute rush before launch. 06 Aug

- ~2.5 million FLOWER deposited in the first ~5 days — roughly a fifth to a quarter of circulating FLOWER. 13 Aug

- OG title: earn 50,000 points within a single week (≈15,000 FLOWER at the week-1 3× multiplier). Once claimed it is permanent; it gets harder each week as the multiplier falls. It is a title, not an item, to avoid incentivising the wrong behaviour. 13 Aug

- The team wants deposited FLOWER spent rather than withdrawn at launch: the first weeks of access will carry discounts on hard-currency items, VIP, hunting events and possibly auctions. 13 Aug

### Leaderboard

- The dashboard leaderboard shows the top 100. 06 Aug

- The team said it would hide the leaderboard closer to launch to stop last-day gaming — no further update since. 06 Aug

- The leaderboard keeps running until the game launches; the lock will be announced about a week before early access. 13 Aug

- The 10 Sep snapshot is what decides the free-mint waves. It is not described as the final airdrop lock. 01 Sep

### Trainer airdrop rewards (13 Aug revision)

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 3. Pre-registration, trainer dashboard and points
chunks.text:
- Rewards were reworked because sign-ups exploded: the top 2,000 (previously top 1,000) now get "something pretty solid"; a new legendary tier was added at the very top; and the former rare tier that ran up to 2,000 supply is now a legendary. Nobody's reward got worse — in many cases it improved. The original announcement was badly worded and read as a nerf. 13 Aug

- Storm and Echo are handed out mostly through the trainer airdrop; a very small amount goes into the in-game Yakkamon rewards pool and some can appear in later special events. 13 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 4. Ronin free mint
chunks.text:
## 4. Ronin free mint

- Chain / platform: Ronin blockchain, via the Ronin Launchpad. Free to mint; you pay gas in RON. Exactly how the launchpad's gas flow works was still unclear (Ronin calls the contract). 01 Sep

- Live: 14 Sep 2026. Contracts were with the Ronin team for review on 1 Sep. 01 Sep

- Supply: 10,000 hidden Yakkamon. 01 Sep (Earlier "10,000–15,000" estimate is superseded.)

- Hidden until 14 Oct 2026. NFTs can be traded on the Ronin marketplace before and after the reveal; once early access begins they can be deposited into the game and used. 13 Aug, 01 Sep

- What's inside: a chance at "some of the legendaries and the early rares" — 3 Storm, 5 Echo, 10 Ghost and 50 Bloom. The stream did not say which of those four are legendary versus early rare, and did not characterise the remainder of the supply. 01 Sep

- The free-mint collection is the Yakkamon collection — Yakkamon released later will appear in the same collection. 01 Sep

- Purpose: hype and exposure on Ronin; pull active players from other Ronin games into Yakkamon. 13 Aug, 01 Sep

- Whitelist rules: rank taken from the yakkamon.com leaderboard at the 10 Sep snapshot. You can mint in more than one wave — the higher your rank, the more chances you get. Within a wave it is first-come: be online, be whitelisted, have RON for gas. Not everyone will get one. 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 4. Ronin free mint
chunks.text:
- Pre-refinement guidance (13 Aug, before the wave table existed): whitelists would be over-provisioned (~20–30% more addresses than NFTs in early waves) so every wave mints out, and everyday players with points could take part. The 1 Sep wave table now defines the actual rank bands. 13 Aug → 01 Sep

- 1,500 also reserved for a manual airdrop, likely a week after the mint and before the reveal. Whether the 1,500 sit inside or outside the 10,000 was not stated. 01 Sep

Waves 01 Sep

| Wave | Who | Supply | Notes |

| 1 | Top 1,000 trainers | — | Guaranteed whitelist spot; mint at your own pace |

| 2 | Top 10,000 trainers | 3,000 | Requires a 5 FLOWER minimum deposit (withdrawable/spendable) — anti-Sybil measure suggested by Ronin; more than 3,000 in the top 10k already qualify |

| 3 | "Ronin wave" — list gathered by the Ronin team from active/top players of other Ronin games | 2,000 | Not tied to the Yakkamon leaderboard; many trainers will still be eligible |

| 4 | Trainers ranked 1–20,000 | — | The wave where the full 10k may mint out |

| 5 | Trainers ranked 1–50,000 | remaining | Only if supply is left |

- Docs: free-mint details and a new Yakopedia section went live in the docs on 1 Sep; a Yakopedia will exist inside the game after launch. 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 5. Rarity tiers, NFTs and the collection
chunks.text:
## 5. Rarity tiers, NFTs and the collection

- Legendary = pre-minted, fixed, very scarce supply. Rare = obtainable only during limited times; supply is not fixed and depends on how players hunt. 13 Aug

- Rarity is set at the species level: every member of a species shares its rarity — there are no rare versions of common monsters. 21 Aug The 1 Sep stream also refers to an uncommon tier ("the rares or the uncommons"). 01 Sep

- Working structure (explicitly not a promise): legendaries are NFTs (close to one-of-ones / incredibly scarce), rares are SFTs, commons are plain game assets. Not every monster is an NFT — only the supply-limited or time-limited ones. 13 Aug

- Once a type of monster has been pre-minted, those are the only ones of that type that can ever exist. New chapters, events and legendaries add new pre-mints to the collection over time (Sunflower Land model). 13 Aug

- Total NFT count is not fixed: 2,000 legendaries via the leaderboard airdrop plus rares, the Ronin free mint, and future additions. 13 Aug

- Legendaries carry traits that only legendaries can have. 13 Aug

- Stats: rares and legendaries get a slightly better stat allotment and higher potential over levelling; the best commons can beat middling rares and roughly match a low-end legendary. Some commons have unique traits too. Rarer monsters have higher impact, more desirable utility and more scarcity. 21 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 5. Rarity tiers, NFTs and the collection
chunks.text: - Forging/merging (e.g. 10 commons → 1 rare): not planned. Bryn dislikes it aesthetically for a cozy creature collector ("squishing your guys into jam") but is "not completely against" it, noting economic positives. Scarcity is handled through contracts and sinks instead. 06 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 6. Legendary utilities (Yakopedia, 1 Sep)
chunks.text:
## 6. Legendary utilities (Yakopedia, 1 Sep)

- Utilities are listed as descriptive text only; numeric values are still being balanced and playtested, and will keep being tuned even after announcement. 01 Sep

- Storm — "Storm-charged": Yakkamon within range work 2× as fast. 01 Sep

- Storm + Echo is called out as a combo worth holding together — "they work together", and with both "you'll be really running through the resource requirements". 01 Sep

- Ghost: the name "Ghost" in the docs drew questions on stream; Adam called it a typo/type swap to be fixed in a docs push, and Bryn said the tier is functionally unchanged — same boosts — with names being aligned to the game's types. Treat the final name as unconfirmed. 01 Sep

- A listed legendary utility regenerates a percentage of max HP every combat turn — described as "absolutely busted" on a monster with good HP/defence; it forces opponents to alpha-strike. 01 Sep

- Farm boosts come from the Yakkamon themselves (no statues to craft or place): legendaries and some rares carry buffing abilities such as 2× on a gathering job. 21 Aug

- AOE sizes: small AOE affects only the jobs immediately around the Yakkamon (e.g. the two or three adjacent trees); large AOE affects an entire section of the farm and every Yakkamon working there. 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 6. Legendary utilities (Yakopedia, 1 Sep)
chunks.text:
- Stacking: boosts with the same name do not stack (two "Wood Gatherer" passives = one); differently named or higher-ranked boosts do stack ("Wood Gatherer" + "Extreme Wood Gatherer"). Some utilities are additive, some multiplicative with each other. Design goal: breadth of different monsters beats duplicates. 21 Aug, 01 Sep

- Rares and uncommons have no utilities listed yet because some of their utilities are randomly rolled when you catch or receive them, alongside the species and stat roll — a monster can have great stats and weak utility or vice versa; the keepers (and the ones worth trading) have both. 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 7. World, land and gathering
chunks.text:
## 7. World, land and gathering

- View and control: top-down "god view" like Sunflower Land; you assign jobs, you do not walk a character around. 01 Sep

- You start on a small revealed patch with one starter Yakkamon; it gathers berries/wood to "part the clouds" into new areas. Clouded areas are unexpanded; some can be glimpsed through. Expanding reveals resource areas (e.g. a lumber yard) and hunting areas. 06 Aug, 13 Aug

- Palworld-style vibe: expand land, collect monsters, put them to work; each Yakkamon fills a role; strong automation focus (Zachtronics-style "set up machines and watch them run"). 06 Aug

- Separate regions: home/gathering regions where you build out, plus distinct hunting regions (desert, beach etc. — the Pokémon "new area" feeling). New regions and monster types arrive chapter by chapter. 21 Aug

- Every Yakkamon you own is another simultaneous action — that is the appeal of expanding your roster. There is no maximum number of active Yakkamon; the pressure is to fully staff all jobs and keep the logistics flowing. 01 Sep

- Logistics puzzle: e.g. one processing building that can make X, Y or Z, each needing wood, crops or ore — you choose what to run and must keep the supply chains for it fed. 01 Sep

- Job cards show growth progress, plot state, completion time and status. 21 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 7. World, land and gathering
chunks.text:
- Upkeep: farm plots have upkeep; soil can show as "degraded" (e.g. 1.6× slower) until re-fertilised, and fertiliser costs resources. Plot groups scale non-linearly: the second and third plots' upkeep grows less than their production, so investing early in efficient plots is rewarded. 21 Aug (How this squares with the 1 Sep "no decay" statement is an open question — see section 17.)

- Absence pauses, it does not punish: if you leave for a week or a month, Yakkamon work until their bins/job areas are full, then stop until you return. There is no decay and no neglect mechanic — the team explicitly rejected an attention system for a 100-Yakkamon farm. 01 Sep

- Resource bins: simplified to one bin per resource (previously many bins). 01 Sep

- Shops: selling resources at shops is in. 01 Sep

- Recipe crafting is being built: resources needed to expand the farm plus lures and baits for hunting. 01 Sep

- Land customisation: likely limited at launch; the team is instead "looking into" full customisation of your own gym (see Combat). More land customisation is expected eventually. 21 Aug

- Time and seasons: an in-game sped-up clock with day/night (not tied to your real clock) so different monsters appear at night; weekly seasons (winter week, summer week…) likely to carry over from Sunflower Land so hunts and farm setups keep changing; a weather system is wanted. 06 Aug, 21 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 7. World, land and gathering
chunks.text: - Current build (1 Sep): about five expansions forming a loop that touches every system; once that is solid, the team builds out the first couple of weeks of gameplay. 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 8. Hunting
chunks.text:
## 8. Hunting

- Hunting is the third pillar alongside gathering and combat, and the primary way to obtain any monster. 06 Aug, 21 Aug

- How it works: hunting is a job. Assign a Yakkamon to a hunting ground; it rolls for a Yakkamon; you influence the outcome with resources (lures, baits). Yakkamon can hunt forever — the limit is the hunting ground, which is progressively hunted out and yields less. 01 Sep

- Hunting grounds have multiple areas (three in the current build; swamps, water areas etc. to come). Tell a Yakkamon to focus on one area (targets that area's monster type — e.g. a rocky outcrop for rock types) or let it wander for anything. Lures attract specific types. 01 Sep

- Two encounter types 01 Sep:

- Aggressive — a red alert on the hunting ground means a monster wants to battle you; most things in that ground pause until you act.

- Ambient — skittish monsters that bop around; you bait them and your hunter has an emoji "conversation" with them until they either join you or run off. Mechanic still being tuned.

- Contracts: requests to find/deliver specific Yakkamon. They are your coin faucet ("your cash faucet for coins") and the main sink for excess Yakkamon — so you will want to hunt very regularly. 06 Aug, 13 Aug, 01 Sep

- Legendaries come mainly through events, tournaments and special conditions; rares can show up in any hunt. 21 Aug

- Seasonal, day/night and calendar systems layer onto hunting so what you can find keeps changing. 06 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 8. Hunting
chunks.text: - Fishing: not designed for early access ("wouldn't be surprised if it ends up in Yakkamon"). 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 9. Combat
chunks.text:
## 9. Combat

- Format: lane-based 3v3. Lanes act top to bottom (lane 1 first). Each Yakkamon has 2–3 abilities in a preset order and cycles through them every time it acts. 01 Sep Positions are chosen before the fight and, as of 21 Aug, could not be changed mid-battle unless a skill does it; AOE attacks make positioning matter. This was not re-confirmed after the 1 Sep player-input decision. 21 Aug

- Player input: NOT a pure simulation. The architecture now lets players take actions during combat via "mechanic swapping" — a major decision made the week of 1 Sep, built flexibly so the battle type can change with player feedback. Real-time interaction mechanics were already being trialled on 21 Aug. 21 Aug, 01 Sep

- Initiative: coin flip, unless a trait decides it; type advantage in a lane supersedes everything and gives that lane the first move — so avoid type disadvantage, especially in lane 1. 01 Sep

- Fight variables: stats, level, type, abilities, passives, potentially a held item. Lane effects, ground types and weather (sandstorm-style) are in the back pocket for later, not early access. 01 Sep

- Types: 13 types at launch (fire, water, rock and familiar archetypes with their own spin). Every Yakkamon has exactly one type at release; multi-types come later. Dragons are only weak to two types instead of three. 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 9. Combat
chunks.text:
- Depth: type advantage vs skill-loop advantage — a favourable matchup can lose to a better skill order (one big hit vs shield-then-attack). Considered cutting skills to two with more passives. 21 Aug

- Build craft: skill expression comes from which monsters you use, their skills, levels, stats and passives; team compositions are long-term projects, not pre-fight retooling. 21 Aug

- Respec / skill extraction: skills can be swapped but respeccing is costly; the intended route is to find a monster with the skill and extract it onto another. 21 Aug

- Pacing: typical fights 3–5 rounds (under a minute), with deliberate variance — some one-turn fights, some longer strategic ones. Battles run on an animation timer that can be sped up, but not skipped entirely if the interactive mechanics ship. 21 Aug

- PvE and PvP use the same system. You can start PvE with only one or two Yakkamon (1v3). 21 Aug, 01 Sep

- PvP: planned as a necessity, arrives post-launch; matchmaking/MMR is essential; no meaningful rewards below an MMR cut-off (anti-bot); sophisticated bots flagged by event tracking. 06 Aug, 21 Aug

- Gyms: the team is looking into a core gym the team hopes you can decorate; visiting players would battle you and see your gym, layout and monsters. 21 Aug

- Expected time split: "a 50/50 split or even a 30/30/30 split" between farming, combat and market/trading/progression — combat is not meant to dominate your time the way it does in Pokémon or RPGs. 21 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 9. Combat
chunks.text:
- Early meta: gathering/economy monsters most sought after; once PvP arenas and tournaments exist the meta likely shifts to battle stats. 21 Aug

- Guilds/alliances: later — core game first. MMO/plaza aspects: wanted, not for early access. 21 Aug, 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 10. Stats, genetics, breeding, evolution, levelling
chunks.text:
## 10. Stats, genetics, breeding, evolution, levelling

- Stats are baked in at generation: each Yakkamon has hidden innate genetic values plus training values. Species have their own stat curves. Age/weight affecting stats was considered and dropped. 06 Aug, 01 Sep

- Build expression = genetics × training × (later) breeding; you shape a monster by investing resources into it, not by equipping gear. 01 Sep

- No wearable gear. At most a single Pokémon-style held item giving one passive. No equipment slots. 01 Sep

- Levelling: through combat, training and food — all of the above. 01 Sep

- Traits/passives: percentage-chance random rolls at catch time; the main way to specialise your farm and combat team. Also obtainable via the market or quests. 06 Aug, 13 Aug

- Breeding: genetics carry down the line; breed good parents of the same species to build bloodlines; 1–3-year breeding projects for optimisers; sneaky ways to move traits across species and type groups. Fixed component + RNG component — you should be able to estimate outcomes within 80–90%. 06 Aug, 13 Aug

- Breeding limits: bred Yakkamon are tradable. To prevent inflation each Yakkamon has a breeding limit scaled by rarity: commons can breed above replacement (two make three), rarer ones roughly replacement, some legendaries only once; offspring inherit a narrower limit. 01 Sep

- Breeding is "coming a bit later"; advanced breeding is post-launch. 06 Aug, 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 10. Stats, genetics, breeding, evolution, levelling
chunks.text:
- Genetics deliberately black-boxed so the community back-solves it together. 06 Aug

- Evolutions: NOT at launch. Reason: with fixed low supply per evolution tier, the population would drift toward the top tier; the team wants to solve that first. When they arrive, conditions are per-monster and partly hidden with in-game hints. 21 Aug, 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 11. Economy
chunks.text:
## 11. Economy

- Free to play, free sign-up. No NFT needed. Guardrails similar to Sunflower Land ("free to try" — put in to get out). 13 Aug, 01 Sep

- Two-layer model (early, "started working on a model"): an unlimited free-to-play layer whose output is untradable; tradable production is gated by spending coins (the Web2 progression currency — possibly renamed "new yen" later). Coin faucets are limited: VIP, economy-positive actions like burning other assets/crops, and Yakkamon contracts. Net effect: F2P is effectively infinite but cannot flood the tradable economy. 01 Sep

- Sinks: contract deliveries consume Yakkamon and will be "hungrier" than generation, so commons get caught and sunk rather than inflating. Heavy sinks everywhere; an infinite end-game sink (as in Sunflower Land's latest chapter). 06 Aug, 13 Aug

- No resets. Mild inflation is accepted as normal; addressed with brakes, hard sinks and new content that absorbs old content (chapter model). 13 Aug

- Marketplace: in-game marketplace confirmed; free-mint NFTs also trade on the Ronin marketplace. 13 Aug

- Skill trading (extract a skill from a monster and sell it) is being considered. 06 Aug

- No enforced producer-vs-fighter capacity split — specialists trade with each other naturally; well-funded players can do both. 21 Aug

- Deposited FLOWER: launch-window discounts, VIP, hunting events and auctions designed to get it spent in-game. 13 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 11. Economy
chunks.text: - Extractive players and botting: below-MMR reward cut-offs and event-tracking bans. 21 Aug (The 13 Aug "export limit" idea is superseded by the two-layer model above.)

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 12. Platform and tech
chunks.text:
## 12. Platform and tech

- Browser web app first; no native app-store release and no console plans for now. Playable on mobile via PWA (add to home screen). 06 Aug, 13 Aug

- Landscape orientation. Main login is email; the PWA is faster than wallet in-app browsers, though the game works in portrait inside wallet browsers when you need a wallet action. 21 Aug

- Login screen and flow built. 01 Sep

- Open source: the client will be open-sourced, but not until the game stabilises — features are still being cut and the team does not want contributors building on things that get removed. Later: translations, patches, UI improvements welcome. 06 Aug, 13 Aug

- A test-environment backdoor that leaked screenshots has been closed. 13 Aug

- Tech built for Yakkamon (audio pipeline, UI/animation effects) will be back-ported to Sunflower Land. 13 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 13. Art, animation and audio
chunks.text:
## 13. Art, animation and audio

- Style: retro bright pixel art in the Sunflower Land family — Yakkamon assets read as a "V2"/HD iteration with better lighting and richer biome patterns, distinct enough to feel like its own game. Base pack is Sunnyside; UI is high-resolution vector with "Nintendo-y" polish. 06 Aug, 21 Aug

- Monsters designed in-house; naming is not finalised — the team wants a naming framework that sounds "Yakkamon" and is open to community suggestions; community memes (e.g. the head-banging sprout) shape monster personality. 13 Aug

- Named/nicknamed so far in streams: Waddler (mouse-like, name not confirmed), a stone turtle Yakkamon, A-Rock (a sleepy, chunky, slow rock monster), the head-banging sprout/"Spud", and a fat hippo silhouette (Bryn's favourite, "probably not going to make it all the way to the end"). 13 Aug, 21 Aug, 01 Sep

- Animation: programmatic animation (hops etc.) at first to avoid huge sprite sheets; not everything animated on day one of early access. Since then an AI tool generates draft animations from still images (A-Rock sleeping, Waddler sniffing around a tree, tree movement) — placeholder quality, to be polished before release. 21 Aug, 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 13. Art, animation and audio
chunks.text:
- Audio: AI-generated by Craig — music, ambient and SFX; each Yakkamon to have its own voice/personality (sleeping snore and select sounds demoed for the turtle and Waddler); farming and battle themes exist in alpha; SFX take ~3.5 min each to generate, music ~3 s; community-made sounds possible if they match fidelity. 13 Aug, 21 Aug

- Lore: not a narrative game, but hints about where monsters came from and who the good/bad guys are will be drip-fed. Community idea that legendaries drive weather/seasons was well received. 21 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 14. Early access scope vs later
chunks.text:
## 14. Early access scope vs later

In early access (fundamentals): gathering/farming, monsters, hunting, basic combat (PvE), core expansions, crafting, shops, Discord integration, 13 types, one type per Yakkamon, legendary utilities. 06 Aug, 21 Aug, 01 Sep

Post-launch / later chapters: PvP arenas and tournaments, advanced breeding, evolutions, multi-types, new regions and monster types each chapter, weather/lane effects, land customisation (gym customisation is the launch-era idea being looked into), guilds, MMO/plaza features, fishing, app-store release (not planned), full animation polish. 06 Aug, 13 Aug, 21 Aug, 01 Sep

Chapter-based rollout is the model: polish the core loops first, then build what the community wants and react to where demand and sinks are needed. 06 Aug

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 15. Community and communication
chunks.text:
## 15. Community and communication

- Wholesome, friendly community norms: no token speculation, degen behaviour or incentive farming; slow mode was needed at peak. 06 Aug

- Streams are weekly-ish Discord team broadcasts. On 6 Aug the team had no recording automation (community members recorded); by 21 Aug the stream opened with "let's get this recording going". 06 Aug, 21 Aug

- Formal proposal process like SFL may come, but base systems will stay partly hidden by design. 06 Aug

- Trivia crossover with the SFL trivia game "perhaps". 21 Aug

- Next showcase intended: the battle system itself. 01 Sep

chunks.title: Dev-stream digest: 16. Open questions / unconfirmed as of 1 Sep
chunks.text:
## 16. Open questions / unconfirmed as of 1 Sep

- Exact wave dates after 14 Sep (tentative, awaiting time-zone feedback) and how gas sponsorship on the Ronin Launchpad works. 01 Sep

- Whether the leaderboard will still be hidden before launch (last stated 6 Aug).

- Which of the free-mint Storm/Echo/Ghost/Bloom counts are legendary versus "early rare", and whether the 1,500 reserve is inside the 10,000. 01 Sep

- Whether soil degradation/upkeep survives as an active-play mechanic now that absence carries no decay. 21 Aug vs 01 Sep

- Numeric values for legendary utilities; exact breeding limits per rarity; the final name of the "coins" currency. 01 Sep

- Whether the ambient-monster taming mechanic survives in its current form. 01 Sep

- Monster names (not finalised). 13 Aug

- Change-linked-wallet feature ETA. 13 Aug

chunks.title: Official docs: About Yakkamon
chunks.text:
About Yakkamon

**Pre-registration is open.** Complete the tasks and increase your points for a chance to win a Legendary Founder NFT.

**Yakkamon is an idle farming automation game that meets an exciting creature collector and battler.**

Venture out across the world to hunt and collect wild monsters, then put them to work gathering resources and farming for you — your farm keeps running while you're away. Catch every creature, craft what you need for battle, build your gym, and grind — or trade — your way to glory. Every core resource and creature is tradable on-chain, so you build your empire your own way.

**Two halves, one game:**

* **The idle half** — your monsters farm, gather, and produce around the clock. Set them up, walk away, come back to progress.
* **The active half** — hunt rare creatures out in the world, craft your gear, and take other trainers on in the arena.

Explore a living world of deserts, volcanoes, and oceans, each region shifting through day and night and changing with the seasons. Every three months, brand-new monsters are released into the wild for players to compete to hunt down and claim.

**Core Game Systems:**

chunks.title: Official docs: About Yakkamon
chunks.text:
* **Idle Farming & Automation:** Put your monsters to work farming and gathering. Production keeps ticking while you're offline, so progress doesn't stop when you log out.
* **Creature Collecting:** Hunt and catch monsters across the wild, then send them out on farming and gathering tasks. Catch them all to build your empire.
* **Regional Exploration:** Journey through deserts, volcanoes, fire regions, and waters, each holding unique resources to gather and craft.
* **Crafting & Hunting:** Refine gathered resources into the gear and items you need to track down and capture rarer, tougher monsters.
* **Day & Night Cycle:** A living world that shifts between day and night, changing what you'll find out in the wild.
* **Seasonal System:** Seasons change the world around you — and every three months, new monsters enter the wild for players to compete over.
* **Arena Battles:** Face off against the best players in PvP arena combat for glory.

chunks.title: Official docs: About Yakkamon — Early access launches November/December 2026
chunks.text:
Early access launches November/December 2026

Early access opens in **November or December 2026**, rolling out in waves. Access is decided by **points**, not by when you signed up — the top 100,000 trainers on the leaderboard get in, and higher ranks enter first (see Early Access and Rewards).

chunks.title: Official docs: About Yakkamon — Built by the Sunflower Land team
chunks.text:
Built by the Sunflower Land team

Yakkamon comes from the team behind **Sunflower Land** — 1M+ players, 100+ open source contributors, and 5+ years of building live and in the open (see The Team).

Sunflower Land is not slowing down — it's on a committed 2-year roadmap, and both games share the same team, the same foundations, and the same token (see FAQ).

chunks.title: Official docs: About Yakkamon — Built on Ronin
chunks.text:
Built on Ronin

* Yakkamon lives on the **Ronin** network.
* We are launching **new NFT collections**, including the Monster NFT drop.
* There is **no new token**. Yakkamon reuses **$FLOWER**, the same token used across our games.

If you want to prepare, you can start collecting **$FLOWER** now. Early deposits earn pre-registration points and can be spent in-game or withdrawn tax-free once you have access to the game (see $FLOWER Deposits).

Built by the team behind Sunflower Land

Yakkamon isn't a first attempt. It's built by the same team that created and still runs **Sunflower Land** — one of the longest-running, most-played on-chain games in the space.

We've been shipping a live game with a real economy, real players, and real money on the line for over five years. Yakkamon is what we're building next.

🎮 Over a million players

Sunflower Land has been played by **more than a million players**. We've built for real players at real scale — through bull markets and bear markets, through launches, seasons, and everything that breaks along the way.

chunks.title: Official docs: The Team — 🏆 People's Choice, Game3 Awards
chunks.text:
🏆 People's Choice, Game3 Awards

Sunflower Land won the **People's Choice award at the Game3 Awards** — voted for by players, not a panel. That's the award we care about most, because it's the one the community decides.

chunks.title: Official docs: The Team — 👩‍💻 100+ open source contributors
chunks.text:
👩‍💻 100+ open source contributors

Over **100 contributors** have shipped code into Sunflower Land. Our players don't just play the game — a lot of them help build it. Features, fixes, translations, and art have come from the community, and that's by design.

chunks.title: Official docs: The Team — ⏳ 5+ years building in the open
chunks.text:
⏳ 5+ years building in the open

We've been building **live and in the open for over five years**. Our code is public, our roadmap is public, and our economy runs where anyone can inspect it. Five years is a long time in web3 gaming — most projects don't make it past their first season.

chunks.title: Official docs: The Team — Why this matters for Yakkamon
chunks.text:
Why this matters for Yakkamon

Launching a game is easy. Running one is hard. A pre-registration campaign is only worth your time if the team behind it will still be here at launch — and long after it.

* **We've done this before.** Sunflower Land is live right now, and has been for years.
* **We're not launching a new token.** Yakkamon reuses **$FLOWER**, the token already at the centre of our existing game economy.
* **We build with our community.** The same open, contributor-driven approach that built Sunflower Land is how we're building Yakkamon.
* **We stick around.** Five years of continuous operation is our answer to "will this project still exist next year?"

Want to see how we build? Go play **Sunflower Land** — it's live today.

chunks.text:

We work with a range of third-party contractors, artists, and designers to make this project possible. Yakkamon's world is inspired by the **Sunnyside** asset pack.

We've also privately contracted and collaborated with Sunnyside artist **Daniel Diggle** on the **monster designs** and the **HD UI art**.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Does Yakkamon mean Sunflower Land gets less attention?
chunks.text:
Does Yakkamon mean Sunflower Land gets less attention?

**No. Sunflower Land is not slowing down — and Yakkamon is part of how it grows.**

We understand the concern. It's a fair thing to ask when a team announces a second game. Here's the honest answer.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Sunflower Land is still shipping
chunks.text:
Sunflower Land is still shipping

In the same six months we've been building Yakkamon, Sunflower Land committed to a **2-year roadmap**, open source contributors have gone **up**, and our release cadence has kept climbing. The work speaks for itself — it's all public, and you can watch it land every week.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — A creature collector doesn't belong inside a farming game
chunks.text:
A creature collector doesn't belong inside a farming game

Sunflower Land is a big, mature, complex game. Bolting a full creature collector onto it would take years and slow both games down. Spinning Yakkamon out as its own project lets us build and iterate far faster — and lets Sunflower Land keep being Sunflower Land.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Both games grow the same ecosystem
chunks.text:
Both games grow the same ecosystem

There is **no new token**. Yakkamon runs on **$FLOWER**, the same token used across our games. More games means more places to use $FLOWER, more players in the ecosystem, and more reasons to be here. This isn't a competing project — it's the same ecosystem getting bigger.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — We're growing the team to meet the demand
chunks.text:
We're growing the team to meet the demand

We're actively looking for more **designers, developers, moderators, and community managers**. Our philosophy hasn't changed: trust the team, keep it lean, and scale when the work calls for it. A lean team is how we've always moved fast, and we add people when it's needed rather than ahead of it.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — 5+ years of shared foundations
chunks.text:
5+ years of shared foundations

This team has worked together for over five years. What takes some projects a year, we can do in three months — because the architecture, tooling, and hard-won lessons carry directly from one game to the other. We're not building things twice.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — AI handles the work that used to eat our time
chunks.text:
AI handles the work that used to eat our time

Recent advances in AI coding have let us streamline a lot of the unglamorous work that used to consume days: migrations, reporting, reward distribution, moderation, and bot detection. That's time going straight back into building both games.

**The short version:** more games, more $FLOWER utility, a bigger team, and shared foundations that make both games faster to build. Sunflower Land is live today — go see for yourself.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Is there a new token?
chunks.text:
Is there a new token?

No. Yakkamon uses **$FLOWER**, the same token used across our games. You can start collecting it now — early deposits earn pre-registration points and can be spent in-game or withdrawn tax-free once you have access (see $FLOWER Deposits).

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — When does Yakkamon launch?
chunks.text:
When does Yakkamon launch?

Early access opens in **November or December 2026**, rolling out in waves. Higher-ranked trainers enter first (see Early Access and Rewards).

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Do I need to be an existing Sunflower Land player?
chunks.text:
Do I need to be an existing Sunflower Land player?

No. Yakkamon is a completely new game and anyone can pre-register with just an email. Sunflower Land players are very welcome, but nothing carries over as a requirement.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — What's the difference between the Monster Egg, the airdrop, and the free mint?
chunks.text:
What's the difference between the Monster Egg, the airdrop, and the free mint?

This is the most common mix-up, so here it is in one place. There are **three separate rewards**, won three different ways:

| | 🥚 **Monster Egg** | 🎁 **Trainer Point airdrop** | 🆓 **Ronin free mint** |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| **How you get it** | Just sign up | Finish top 5,000 on points | Mint it on the Ronin launchpad in mid-September |
| **How many** | Up to 500,000 | 5,000 | **Coming soon** |
| **Decided by** | Sign-up order | Your points rank | Verified whitelist — one mint per trainer |
| **Is it an NFT?** | **No** | Yes | Yes |
| **Need a wallet?** | **No** | Yes | Yes |
| **How it reaches you** | Appears on your farm when you log in | Airdropped at early access | Minted to your wallet in mid-September |

**You can have all three.** They don't compete and one doesn't replace another. Signing up gets you an egg, earning points can get you an airdrop, and minting in mid-September can get you a minted monster.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Is my sign-up Monster Egg an NFT?
chunks.text:
Is my sign-up Monster Egg an NFT?

**No.** The egg you get for signing up is an in-game item, not an NFT. You don't mint it, you don't need a wallet for it, and it isn't part of the free mint or the NFT Airdrop. It just appears on your farm the first time you log into the game.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — How many can be minted in the free mint?
chunks.text:
How many can be minted in the free mint?

**Coming soon.** We're still finalising it. The free mint is launching via the **Ronin launchpad**, and we're working directly with the Ronin team on the **whitelist**, the **wave structure** and the **total supply** — including the anti-sybil checks that keep bots and multi-accounts out. We'll announce all of it well ahead of mint day (see Free Mint).

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Do I need to mint to get my Monster Egg?
chunks.text:
Do I need to mint to get my Monster Egg?

**No.** They're unrelated. Your egg is already yours from signing up and arrives on your farm automatically. The free mint is a separate, optional event in mid-September for a different thing — an NFT monster.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Does signing up early get me early access?
chunks.text:
Does signing up early get me early access?

**No.** Signing up early gets you one thing: a better **egg type**. It does not give you early access, reserve a spot, guarantee a Monster NFT, or put you ahead of anyone on the leaderboard.

Early access goes to the **top 100,000 trainers on points**. To get in — and to get in early — you have to earn points and climb (see Early Access and Rewards).

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — So what does signing up early actually get me?
chunks.text:
So what does signing up early actually get me?

A better egg tier, and nothing more:

| Sign-up position | Monster Egg |
| --------------------- | ----------- |
| **1 – 10,000** | 💎 Platinum |
| **10,001 – 25,000** | 🥇 Gold |
| **25,001 – 50,000** | 🥈 Silver |
| **50,001 – 100,000** | 🥉 Bronze |
| **100,001 – 500,000** | Basic |

A Platinum egg is a nicer starting egg. It is not a head start on the leaderboard.

**These eggs are not NFTs and they are not airdropped.** Your Monster Egg simply appears on your farm the first time you log into the game — there's nothing to claim and no wallet needed. It is completely separate from the NFT Airdrop.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — I signed up late — did I miss out?
chunks.text:
I signed up late — did I miss out?

No. Your egg tier is set, but everything that matters is still fully open to you. Rank is earned, not reserved — a Basic egg holder who earns points daily will finish above a Platinum egg holder who signed up first and never came back.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Is the NFT airdrop first come, first served?
chunks.text:
Is the NFT airdrop first come, first served?

No. The **5,000 Monster NFTs** go to the top 5,000 trainers on the **points leaderboard**, not the first 5,000 to sign up (see NFT Airdrop).

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Did the 12 August update make my rank worth less?
chunks.text:
Did the 12 August update make my rank worth less?

**No.** No leaderboard rank came away with a weaker monster than it was already in line for.

What changed is that the tiers got **wider** and the monsters got **better**. Lower-tier Yakkamon utility is being lifted to match the traits players were already expecting, and the old 501–1,000 band widened to **501–2,000** — so Legendaries now run twice as deep down the leaderboard as they used to.

The one genuinely new addition is **Storm**, airdropped to the top 50. It was added *above* the top of the old ladder rather than pushing anyone down it: the monster that used to sit at the top is now called **Echo**, and everyone in the top 50 was upgraded past it onto Storm.

See the full before-and-after in NFT Airdrop. Monster utilities are revealed in **September**.

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — What is the egg counter on the pre-registration page?
chunks.text:
What is the egg counter on the pre-registration page?

That's the **Monster Egg** counter — it's tracking egg tiers only. It is not an early-access counter and it is not counting down Monster NFTs. When a tier fills up, the only thing you've missed is that egg type (see Early Access and Rewards).

chunks.title: Official docs: Official FAQ — Which network is Yakkamon on?
chunks.text:
Which network is Yakkamon on?

**Ronin** — the same network the Monster NFT free mint runs on (see Free Mint).

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards
chunks.text:
Early Access and Rewards

**Pre-registration is open now.** Sign up with just an email to claim your **Monster Egg** — then start earning points.

Pre-registration works in two steps:

1. **Sign up** with just an email — this gets you a **Monster Egg**, and nothing else.
2. **Earn points** — this is what decides your trainer number, your early-access wave, and your Monster NFT.

**Signing up early does not get you early access.** It does not reserve a spot, guarantee a place in Wave 1, or put you ahead of anyone. The **only** thing sign-up order decides is which **egg type** you get. Everything that actually matters is earned on the leaderboard.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — Monster Egg tiers
chunks.text:
Monster Egg tiers

Sign-up order decides one thing: your egg type. Tiers are handed out in the order people register — once a tier is gone, it's gone.

| Sign-up position | Monster Egg |
| --------------------- | ----------- |
| **1 – 10,000** | 💎 Platinum |
| **10,001 – 25,000** | 🥇 Gold |
| **25,001 – 50,000** | 🥈 Silver |
| **50,001 – 100,000** | 🥉 Bronze |
| **100,001 – 500,000** | Basic |

A Platinum egg is a nicer starting egg. It is **not** a head start on the leaderboard, and it does not carry any claim on early access.

**Your Monster Egg is not an NFT.** It's an in-game item — there's nothing to mint, nothing to claim, and no wallet needed. It simply **appears on your farm** the first time you log into Yakkamon.

**Late to sign up? You can still finish at the top.** A Basic egg holder who earns points daily will finish above a Platinum egg holder who signs up and never comes back. Rank is earned, not reserved.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — The three things people mix up
chunks.text:
The three things people mix up

There are **three separate rewards**. They're won in three different ways and they reach you in three different ways.

| | 🥚 **Monster Egg** | 🎁 **Trainer Point airdrop** | 🆓 **Ronin free mint** |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| **How you get it** | Just sign up | Finish top 5,000 on points | Mint it on the Ronin launchpad in mid-September |
| **How many** | Up to 500,000 | 5,000 | **Coming soon** |
| **Decided by** | Sign-up order | Your points rank | Verified whitelist — one mint per trainer |
| **Is it an NFT?** | **No** | Yes | Yes |
| **Need a wallet?** | **No** | Yes | Yes |
| **How it reaches you** | Appears on your farm when you log in | Airdropped at early access | Minted to your wallet in mid-September |

**You can have all three.** They don't compete and one doesn't replace another. Signing up gets you an egg, earning points can get you an airdrop, and minting in mid-September can get you a minted monster.

Read more about the Ronin free mint and the NFT Airdrop.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — What points decide
chunks.text:
What points decide

Everything below is decided by **points only** — never by when you signed up:

1. **Your trainer number** — your permanent rank among the founding players.
2. **Whether you get early access at all** — and which wave you join. Higher ranks enter the game first.
3. **What you're airdropped at launch** — including the Monster NFTs.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — Earning points
chunks.text:
Earning points

You earn points by taking part in the community and getting ready for launch. For example:

* **Daily nurture** — tap your egg each day, with bonuses for keeping a streak.
* **Quests** — link your Discord and Twitter, post weekly, and contribute in the community.
* **Refer friends** — earn points for each verified friend who signs up. Your first five are instant; after that your friend needs to verify Discord and Twitter and reach 100 points (see Referral rules).
* **Free mint** — mint the Monster NFT on Ronin (see Free Mint).
* **Early $FLOWER deposits** — deposit $FLOWER to convert it into points. Bigger deposits earn exponentially more, and your $FLOWER can be spent in-game or withdrawn tax-free once you have game access (see $FLOWER Deposits).

**Daily actions compound.** Streak bonuses and referrals stack over time, so the earlier you start *earning*, the harder your rank is to overtake. Signing up and going quiet earns you nothing — the points only come from showing up.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — Referral rules
chunks.text:
Referral rules

**Unverified and multi-account referrals will be removed.** Only genuine, verified referrals count toward your final rewards.

Referrals are reviewed before rewards are finalised. A referral only counts if the friend is a real, separate person with a verified account who actually engages with pre-registration.

#### When a referral qualifies

To stop temporary email sign-ups and bot accounts from farming referral points, your friend must do all of the following before you receive the points:

1. **Verify their Discord** — link a Discord account to their trainer profile.
2. **Verify their Twitter** — link a Twitter/X account to their trainer profile.
3. **Reach 100 points** in their trainer dashboard.

**Your first five referrals are instant.** Points for referrals 1–5 are awarded as soon as your friend signs up. From your sixth referral onward, the three steps above must be completed before the points land.

The following will **not** count toward your points, rank, or final rewards:

* **Unverified accounts** — sign-ups that never complete verification.
* **Multi-accounting** — referring yourself using alt accounts, throwaway emails, or shared devices and wallets.
* **Bots and automation** — bulk or scripted sign-ups.
* **Inactive sign-ups** — accounts created solely to farm a referral bonus that show no real activity.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — Referral rules
chunks.text: Referral points are provisional until the final review. Removed referrals are deducted from your total, which can lower your trainer number and your tier. Serious or repeated abuse can disqualify an account from pre-registration rewards entirely.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — Reward track
chunks.text:
Reward track

Every **7 days**, a new list of rewards appears for you to claim. Claimed items are added straight to your inventory and stay there — and once you gain early access, you'll be able to claim them in game.

**Check back weekly.** Each new reward list replaces the last, so log in every 7 days to keep collecting.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — Early Access — November/December 2026
chunks.text:
Early Access — November/December 2026

**Only the top 100,000 trainers on points will get early access.** Pre-registering does not qualify you — you have to finish inside the top 100,000 on the leaderboard. Everyone below rank 100,000 misses out and has to wait for full launch.

Trainer numbers and tiers are revealed shortly before early access begins. Your **points rank** — not your sign-up date — decides which **egg** you receive and which early-access wave you join. Higher tiers enter the game first.

Early access is the head start: build your gathering empire, catch the basic creatures, and get your resources and equipment ready before **Chapter 0** opens the game up a month later (see Important Dates).

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — The Genesis Legendaries
chunks.text:
The Genesis Legendaries

The top **2,000** trainers each receive one of the **four Genesis Legendaries** — the founding set. Ranks 2,001 to 5,000 receive a **Rare Egg**.

| Points rank | Reward |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- |
| **1 – 3** | 🌩️ **Storm** + 🌫️ **Echo** |
| **4 – 10** | 🌩️ **Storm** + 👻 **Ghost** |
| **11 – 50** | 🌩️ **Storm** |
| **51 – 250** | 🌫️ **Echo** |
| **251 – 500** | 👻 **Ghost** |
| **501 – 2,000** | 🌸 **Bloom** |
| **2,001 – 5,000** | Rare Egg |
| **5,001+** | ❌ No airdrop |

**Storm is the newest monster in the set**, and the hardest to earn — it sits above everything else, and in this airdrop it goes to the top 50. The top **10** trainers receive Storm *and* a second Genesis Legendary alongside it.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — What changed on 12 August
chunks.text:
What changed on 12 August

We widened the tiers and added a new monster at the very top. Every band either kept the monster it was already in line for or moved **up** into a better one — Storm was added *above* the old ladder rather than pushing anyone down it.

| Points rank | Previously | Now | What changed |
| ----------------- | --------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **1 – 3** | Legendary Egg A | 🌩️ Storm + 🌫️ Echo | Echo **is** the old Legendary A. Storm is new, and stacks on top of it. |
| **4 – 10** | Legendary Egg A | 🌩️ Storm + 👻 Ghost | Storm outclasses the old Legendary A — and Ghost comes with it. |
| **11 – 50** | Legendary Egg A | 🌩️ Storm | Straight upgrade to the new top-tier monster. |
| **51 – 100** | Legendary Egg A | 🌫️ Echo | The same monster as before, with its utility lifted. |
| **101 – 250** | Legendary Egg B | 🌫️ Echo | Moved **up** into what used to be the top tier. |
| **251 – 500** | Legendary Egg B | 👻 Ghost | Same slot, utility lifted. |
| **501 – 1,000** | Legendary Egg C | 🌸 Bloom | Same slot, utility lifted to what the tier above was expecting. |
| **1,001 – 2,000** | Rare Egg | 🌸 Bloom | The old 501–1,000 band **widened to 501–2,000**. Rare becomes Legendary. |
| **2,001 – 5,000** | Rare Egg | Rare Egg | Unchanged |

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — What changed on 12 August
chunks.text:
**Twice as many Legendaries.** Legendary monsters used to stop at rank 1,000. They now run all the way to rank **2,000** — twice as far down the leaderboard as before.

**Nothing has been nerfed.** This update does **not** nerf an existing Yakkamon for a leaderboard ranking. Lower-tier Yakkamon utility is being **lifted** to match previously expected traits, and we're releasing **more monsters** — so every rank still gets the kind of monster utility it was already in line for, and a thousand more trainers now hold a Legendary. We'll be releasing the monster utilities in **September**, so stay tuned!

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — Early access waves
chunks.text:
Early access waves

Early access opens in **waves**, and your points rank decides which one you're in. Higher ranks play first — Wave 1 trainers are in the game before anyone in Wave 2 has logged in, and each wave follows a week after the one before it (see Important Dates).

| Points rank | Early access |
| -------------------- | ----------------- |
| **1 – 1,000** | Wave 1 |
| **1,001 – 5,000** | Wave 2 |
| **5,001 – 20,000** | Wave 3 |
| **20,001 – 100,000** | Wave 4 |
| **100,001+** | ❌ No early access |

**Your wave and your monster are set by the same leaderboard, but they don't line up one-to-one.** Wave 1 runs to rank 1,000 while the airdrop runs to rank 5,000 — so a trainer at rank 900 is in the first wave holding a Bloom, and a trainer at rank 1,500 also holds a Bloom but joins in Wave 2. Climbing improves both.

chunks.title: Official docs: Early Access and Rewards — The NFT airdrop
chunks.text:
The NFT airdrop

Every monster in the table above is a **Monster NFT**, airdropped to the top **5,000** trainers — a Genesis Legendary for the top 2,000, and a Rare Egg from there to 5,000.

These are among the strongest monsters in the game, they're fully tradable, and they're revealed live at early access launch. This airdrop will never run again.

Read the full breakdown in 🎁 NFT Airdrop.

---

chunks.title: Official docs: Important Dates
chunks.text:
Important Dates

Everything scheduled between now and early access, in one place.

| Event | Timing |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **$FLOWER deposits open** — 3× points week | Live now (since 10 Aug), stepping down 0.2× per week to 1× |
| **Monster and egg utilities revealed** | September |
| **Ronin free mint** — on the Ronin blockchain via the Ronin launchpad | 14th September — whitelists finalised 10th September (free mint only, not the trainer airdrop) |
| **Free mint reveal** | 14th October (one month after the mint) |
| **Leaderboard finalises** | One week before early access launch |
| **Airdrop rewards sent out** | Three days after the leaderboard finalises |
| **Early access launch** | November / December — exact date to be announced |
| **Wave 1 enters** | Early access launch day |
| **Wave 2 enters** | One week after Wave 1 |
| **Wave 3 enters** | One week after Wave 2 |
| **Wave 4 enters** | Confirmed closer to launch |
| **Chapter 0 launch** | One month after early access launch |

**The leaderboard finalises one week before early access launch.** The rank you hold at that moment is the rank your rewards are calculated on — points earned after it cannot change your tier, your monster, or your wave.

chunks.title: Official docs: Important Dates
chunks.text: **We will announce the exact date and give you plenty of notice beforehand.** Nobody is going to wake up to a leaderboard that locked overnight.

chunks.title: Official docs: Important Dates — What's available in early access
chunks.text:
What's available in early access

Early access is your head start. You'll be able to start building your **gathering empire**, catch the **basic creatures**, and prepare your resources and equipment for the Chapter 0 start.

That's a genuine advantage — time to set up, prepare, and get used to the game before the rest of the world arrives. It isn't a permanent one, though: players who come in at **Chapter 0** can still catch up with enough effort.

chunks.title: Official docs: Important Dates — Chapter 0 — one month after early access
chunks.text:
Chapter 0 — one month after early access

Chapter 0 is when the game opens up properly. By then everyone from pre-registration has been let into the game, and the systems that needed to be securely set up and tested go live:

* **The first official NFT monster hunt** begins.
* **The first batch of Legendaries** is released.
* **Auctions** open — bid your $FLOWER on rare and one-off items.
* **$FLOWER withdrawals & the marketplace opens** begin.

**Why these wait for Chapter 0.** Auctions, withdrawals and the Legendaries are deliberately held back until everyone from pre-registration is in the game and everything has been securely set up and tested. Nobody ends up competing against a system only part of the playerbase can reach.

chunks.title: Official docs: Important Dates — What this means for you
chunks.text:
What this means for you

* **Deposit sooner rather than later.** The points multiplier on $FLOWER deposits is at its highest right now and steps down every week, so the same deposit is worth less the longer you leave it.
* **Climb before the lock.** Everything that decides your reward — your monster, your wave, your trainer number — is settled the moment the leaderboard finalises.
* **Rewards land three days later.** Your airdrop arrives shortly after the lock, ahead of launch day.
* **Utilities come first.** What each monster actually does is revealed in **September**, well before the leaderboard finalises — so you will know what you're climbing toward.

**Dates firm up as we get closer.** Timings on this page are our current plan, and anything without a fixed date will be confirmed and announced in advance.
